audits.name: Misner-Sharp mass identity Gamma^2 - U^2 = g^ab d_aR d_bR = 1 - 2m/R (Misner & Sharp 1964, via Hayward gr-qc/9408002 eq. (27))

source.located: C. W. Misner & D. H. Sharp, Phys. Rev. 136, B571 (1964), no arXiv copy. Restated by S. A. Hayward, 'Gravitational energy in spherical symmetry', PRD 53, 1938 (1996), arXiv gr-qc/9408002v2: eq.(4) p.4, eqs.(23)-(28) pp.11-12, eqs.(31)-(35) pp.12-13, Prop.1 p.4, App.B p.19, ref.[4] p.22. An independent second restatement: A. Escriva arXiv:2504.05813v3 eqs.(2.2)-(2.5), (2.24), refs.[50],[57] = MS 1964. Later context: Maeda & Nozawa arXiv:0709.1199v4 eq.(2.7), ref.[6].
source.via: alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries on gr-qc/9408002 plus get_paper_content fullText. The extracted text had lost its Greek letters; they were recovered by decoding the TeX OML font bytes (0x15=lambda, 0x10=zeta, 0x1C=tau). pi and rho decode to physically correct places, which validates the map. Also answer_pdf_queries on 2504.05813 and 0709.1199. Misner & Sharp 1964 and Hernandez & Misner 1966 are NAMED-NOT-READ: the arxiv.org e-print fetch got a proxy 403.

audits.published_statement: Hayward gr-qc/9408002 p.4 eq.(4): 'The Misner-Sharp spherically symmetric gravitational energy ... may be defined in units G = 1 by E = (1/2) r (1 - g^{-1}(dr,dr)) = (1/2) r + e^f r d+r d-r = (1/2) r + (1/4) e^f r^3 theta+ theta-. The form actually given by Misner & Sharp is derived in Section IV. Note that E is an invariant. Indeed, the only invariants of the metric and its first derivatives are functions of r and E.' pp.11-12 eqs.(23)-(27): coordinates (tau, zeta) with g(d_tau,d_zeta) = 0, g(d_tau,d_tau) = -1, 'Define a function lambda by e^lambda = g(d_zeta,d_zeta)', ds^2 = r^2 dOmega^2 + e^lambda dzeta^2 - dtau^2 (26), '1 - 2E/r = e^{-lambda}(r')^2 - rdot^2 (27) which is the form actually given by Misner & Sharp [4], with different notation.' Prop.1: trapped iff E > r/2, marginal iff E = r/2, untrapped iff E < r/2. App.B: E is the Kodama charge. Escriva 2504.05813 eqs.(2.3),(2.5): U = (1/A) dR/dt, Gamma = (1/B) dR/dr, Gamma = sqrt(1 + U^2 - 2M/R), attributed to MS [57] in the general-lapse comoving metric.
published_hypotheses: Spherical symmetry, 'assumed implicitly in the Propositions' (Hayward p.2).
r is the areal radius (area 4 pi r^2), r > 0 (Hayward p.3).
The spacetime is time-orientable (Hayward p.3). This is needed for the SIGNS of theta^pm, not for E.
Units G = 1, c = 1.
Definition (4) uses no field equation. The Einstein equations with no cosmological constant enter only in the variation formulas (10)-(11) and (28).
Form (27) is written in a lapse-1, zero-shift gauge adapted to a spatial hypersurface Sigma (eqs.23a,b). For (27) and (28) the gauge is needed only on Sigma.
Misner & Sharp's own setting: adiabatic perfect fluid, comoving coordinates, general lapse (Hayward p.12; Escriva eqs.2.1-2.3).
The enclosed-integral form E = int 4 pi r^2 rho r' dzeta (eq.33) needs a regular centre. The definition does not.
hypothesis_drift: DISCREPANCY IN A QUOTATION (a misprint, not a refutation). driven.py:56-58 quotes Hayward eq.(27) as 'e^{-chi}(r')^2'. The v2 text prints e^{-lambda}, where lambda is the metric function of eq.(24); the coordinates are (tau, zeta) and no chi appears in eqs.(23)-(27). Reading chi as a coordinate would make the equation false (rederive C11b, residual nonzero). The tree's working identity is correct: driven.py V3 (driven.py:571-574) and foliation.py V1 (:637-640) use e^{-2Lambda}, which is Hayward's form at lambda = 2 Lambda, Phi = 0 (C2b, residual 0). foliation.py:381-383 and :875-876 cite the equation by number only. Recorded, nothing repaired.

BROADENED, and supported: lapse-1 gauge to general lapse. Hayward's (27) uses the lapse-1 gauge; driven.py:145, foliation.py:632 and nonstatic.py:26 use e^{2Phi}. driven.py:65-66 translates correctly. Checked: C1 (any diagonal lapse), C1b (with a shift), C5a-c (Schwarzschild gives E = M in the Schwarzschild, Lemaitre and Painleve-Gullstrand charts). The diagonal 'general metric' is without loss of generality locally.

BROADENED, and supported: MS's comoving perfect fluid to general matter with radial flux j (nonstatic.py:28-30, formation.py:130-136). Definition (4) is geometric, and Hayward's (28a),(28b) were re-derived from G_ab = 8 pi T_ab, residual 0 (C7).

ADDED GLOSS: 'enclosed' Misner-Sharp mass (ledger.py:337, 367 D1). Hayward p.17 says E is 'a function of spheres only'. The enclosed integral (33) needs a regular centre, the Einstein equations, and Lambda = 0 (Maeda-Nozawa eq.2.7). The sign theorems the tree rests on need none of these (C8b). Where there is no regular centre, m encloses nothing: throatmass.py's own throat (m = r_0/2, the marginal case of Prop.1) and M < 0 Schwarzschild are examples. A wording drift; it moves no verdict.

UNSTATED Lambda = 0 where m is tied to matter: throatmass.py:235 (rho = -G^t_t/8pi) and tolman.py:705 (m = 4 pi R^3 p_r). formation.py:124-126 names H_EFE G_ab = 8 pi T_ab. Maeda-Nozawa eq.(2.7) shows the Lambda-generalised mass differs. Harmless if vacuum energy is counted in rho or p_r.

WORDING, minor: foliation.py:857 ONLY_INVARIANT leaves out Hayward's discrete invariants (the signs of theta^pm, p.3). The range theorem already respects them through the untrapped orientation (foliation.py:134-136), so INVARIANT_CRITERION (:858) is unaffected.

NO DRIFT (checked): hpscentre.py:644-645 and throatmass.py:20 use m = (r/2)(1 - r'^2), which needs U = 0. Both metrics are static (throatmass.py:214-215). formation.py:110 names H_U0. overturn.py:124-127 matches Hayward's scope; Hayward p.17 names the Hawking energy as the extension beyond spherical symmetry.

What was checked: C1 and C1b: the scalar equals Gamma^2 - U^2 for a diagonal metric and (n.dR)^2 - (u.dR)^2 with a shift. C2 and C2b: Hayward (26)->(27), and the tree form equals Hayward's. C3: Hayward eq.(4) in double-null form. C4: boost invariance. C5: Schwarzschild E = M in 3 charts. C8 (z3): Gamma > 1 <=> U^2 R > 2m proved unsat; at U = 0, Gamma > 1 <=> m < 0 proved unsat; Gamma > 1 with m > 0 is SAT when U != 0. C9: Escriva (2.24) equals tree V2. later_literature.what: Restates MS exactly as eq.(27); E is invariant; trapping iff E > r/2; E is the Kodama charge; general-matter variation formulas (28). Eqs.(4), (27) and (28) were machine-checked here.
A second, independent attribution of U, Gamma and Gamma = sqrt(1+U^2-2M/R) to MS 1964 in the general-lapse gauge. Gamma < 0 at type-II necks, which is consistent with the tree's untrapped Gamma > 0.

Generalised MS mass with Lambda and Gauss-Bonnet (eq.2.7), which reduces to MS in 4D with Lambda = 0. Notes a gap in Hayward's positivity proof, which the tree does not use, and that the MS mass is not the only quasi-local mass (Brown-York differs).
The MS-type mass becomes theory-dependent in f(R), massive gravity and under conformal maps. The tree works in GR, so there is no narrowing.

audits.lacked_data: Tested for this result, M's hypothesis finds nothing. The identity has no empirical input: it is the definition 1 - 2m/R = g^ab d_aR d_bR plus 2-metric algebra, so no datum Misner & Sharp could have lacked bears on it. It was re-derived from scratch here: residual 0 in 10 forms and 3 Schwarzschild charts, with vacuity guards. What 1964 lacked was conceptual, not data: the Kodama vector (1980), Hayward's invariant and trapping formulation with E as the Kodama charge (1994-96), the Lambda and higher-curvature generalisations (2008), and the exotic geometries where m < 0 or no regular centre occurs. Each of these reproduces the identity unchanged. The only moved-datum candidate anywhere in the tree's use is G in the SI exchange rate, and CODATA 2022 left G identical to 2018. The evidence against M's hypothesis is complete for this result. Later work sharpens only the tree's 'enclosed' gloss (it needs a regular centre, EFE and Lambda = 0), which is recorded as a drift.
audits.grade_evidence: The statement was read in Hayward eqs.(4) and (27) and in Escriva eq.(2.5): exactly the tree's Gamma^2 - U^2 = g^ab dR dR = 1 - 2m/R, attributed to MS 1964 by two independent restatements. On hypotheses, the tree uses the source's own class (spherical symmetry plus areal radius), with untrapped, U = 0 and H_EFE named where they are used. Its broader use (general lapse, general matter) was machine-checked (C1, C1b, C5, C7). The re-derivation agrees, 24/24 with vacuity guards. No datum enters, and G is unchanged in CODATA 2022. Four discrepancies are recorded, not repaired, and none moves a verdict: (i) driven.py:58 misprints Hayward's e^{-lambda} as e^{-chi}; (ii) 'enclosed' at ledger.py:337, 367 is an added gloss; (iii) Lambda = 0 is unstated at throatmass.py:235 and tolman.py:705; (iv) foliation.py:857 ONLY_INVARIANT leaves out the discrete sign invariants. MS 1964 itself remains NAMED-NOT-READ. For a definition, two restatements plus an independent derivation are enough for it to stand.
audits.what_would_change_the_grade: NARROWED if a tree verdict is shown to use the 'enclosed' (volume-integral) reading on a slice with no regular centre, or with Lambda != 0 and vacuum energy excluded from rho. None was found at the owner sites read. Reading MS 1964 at source and finding a relation that differs from Hayward (27) and Escriva (2.5) beyond notation would be a DISCREPANCY in the attribution, not WRONG. WRONG would need a nonzero residual in the closed-form checks C1/C2.

verifiers.reason:
I could not refute the grade in either direction.

**How the source was read.** The alphaXiv quota was exhausted, and arxiv.org and semanticscholar returned a proxy CONNECT 403. So I read Hayward gr-qc/9408002v2 from the cached extraction at scratchpad/d67/src/casmag/all/gr-qc_9408002v2.txt, at byte level:
- Eq.(24) is 'e\n\x15 = g(@=@\x10;@=@\x10)'. In the standard OML font 0x15 is lambda and 0x10 is zeta, so this reads e^lambda = g(d_zeta, d_zeta).
- Eq.(27) is '1 - 2E/r = e^{-\x15}(r')^2 - rdot^2'. The minus signs survive only as spaces, the same way as in '=  1' of (23b).
- The whole text holds zero 0x1F (chi) bytes. So driven.py:58's e^{-chi} is a quotation discrepancy, as the audit says. The tree's working form e^{-2Lambda}R'^2 - e^{-2Phi}Rdot^2 (driven.py:571-574, foliation.py:637-640) is correct.

**Other claims checked at source.**
- Hayward p.2 'implicitly in the Propositions', p.3 time-orientable, Prop.1 (trapped iff E > r/2), and p.12 'the form actually given by Misner & Sharp [4], with different notation' are all confirmed.
- Escriva 2504.05813v3 eqs.(2.2), (2.3) and (2.5) (general lapse, U = D_tR, Gamma = D_rR, Gamma = sqrt(1+U^2-2M/R)) are confirmed, with refs [50] and [57] = Misner & Sharp.

**The computation.** I re-ran rederive/misner-sharp-1964.py: ALL PASS, exit 0. The z3 check C8 assumes Gamma > 0, which is the named untrapped orientation.

**Why STANDS holds.** The result is a definition plus 2-metric algebra with no empirical input. No moved datum can reach it. G is identical in CODATA 2018 and 2022, and G enters only the SI exchange rate.

**One correction to the audit, in the direction against the tree. It does not move the grade.** Drift note (ii) calls 'enclosed' Misner-Sharp mass (ledger.py:337, 367) an 'ADDED GLOSS'. But the audit's own second restatement, Escriva eq.(2.4), introduces the Misner-Sharp mass as exactly that enclosed integral, M = int_0^R 4 pi R~^2 rho dR~. So 'enclosed' is a standard usage in the source restatements, not a gloss the tree invented. The attached hypotheses (regular centre, H_EFE, Lambda = 0) are correct, and overturn.py:40-52 (link L2) already names the regular-centre requirement explicitly. L3's deficit integral uses m(r) directly, not the enclosed form.

**What stays open.** Misner & Sharp 1964 itself remains NAMED-NOT-READ. A reading at source could only produce an attribution discrepancy, not a change to this grade. verifiers.lens: RE-RUN THE RE-DERIVATION: re-ran the audit's sympy/z3 script from a copy, checked what each check actually encodes against the published statement, and ran vacuity guards with the hypotheses negated and the encodings mutated.
verifiers.reason:
I ran a copy of the script at /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Claude-Method-Works/6d820e7d-6d3c-5ac7-8067-527dc14c2847/scratchpad/d67/verify/rederive/misner-sharp-1964.py under sympy 1.14.0 and z3 4.x (5.1.0 string). It gives ALL PASS, 24/24, exit 0, in about 6 s, which matches the audit's claim. Output is in misner-sharp-1964.rerun.out.

ENCODING. The checks test the actual statement, not a toy version of it.
- C1 builds g^ab d_aR d_bR from the inverse of a fully general 4-metric -e^{2Phi(t,r)}dt^2 + e^{2Lambda(t,r)}dr^2 + R(t,r)^2 dOmega^2, and C1b adds a shift. It reduces the result to Gamma^2 - U^2. This is the tree's V1 in generality.
- C2 computes E from Hayward's eq.(4) definition in his (26) gauge and recovers (27) with e^{-lambda}. C2b maps it to the tree form at lambda = 2 Lambda, Phi = 0.
- C5 gives Schwarzschild E = M in three charts. The Lemaitre metric and the Painleve-Gullstrand metric are both encoded correctly.
- C7 re-derives the variation formulas from a full Christoffel -> Ricci -> Einstein computation. In the perfect-fluid limit (T00 = rho, T01 = 0, T11 = p e^lambda) its form reduces to the known Misner-Sharp equations m' = 4 pi r^2 rho r' and mdot = -4 pi r^2 p rdot, so the content is right.
- C8's z3 statements are the tree's actual sign theorems, with the hypotheses R > 0 and Gamma > 0 (untrapped) explicit.

VACUITY. My own guards are in guards.py and guards.out: 13/13 as expected.
- Dropping Gamma > 0 makes both C8a and C8b refutable. The witness is G = -2, U = 0, m = -3/2, R = 1.
- R < 0 makes C8b refutable.
- Dropping U = 0 makes C8b refutable.
- The C8b hypothesis set is itself satisfiable, so the unsat result is not vacuous.
- A sign-flipped identity breaks C8a.
- Dropping the lapse from U breaks C1, and so does using e^{-Lambda} in place of e^{-2Lambda}.
- Schwarzschild with E = M/2 is nonzero.

INDEPENDENT CROSS-CHECKS, not in the audit. Reissner-Nordstrom gives E = M - Q^2/(2r), and flat FLRW with the Friedmann density gives E = (4pi/3) rho R^3. Both have residual 0.

WEAKNESSES FOUND. None moves the grade.
- C9 is a tautology. Substituting M = (R/2)(1 + U^2 - Gamma^2) back into Gamma^2 = 1 + U^2 - 2M/R vanishes by rearrangement alone, which my T1 confirms for bare symbols. So C9 does not independently check Escriva's gauge. C1 covers that content anyway, with A = e^Phi and B = e^Lambda.
- C10 hardcodes G22 = G18. That the two agree is a READ claim from CODATA 2022, not a computation. The arithmetic c^2/(G*LAMBDA) = 1.348948e26 does reproduce, with LAMBDA = overturn.LAMBDA = 9.982529174194637, as used at ledger.py:334-343.
- C4 is only the algebraic boost identity.
- The misprint the audit records is real. driven.py:59 reads e^{-chi}, and C11b shows a literal reading would be false. The working identity in the tree is correct.

LIMIT. I could not re-read Hayward's printed eqs.(27)-(28) at source myself: the alphaXiv call returned 'quota exceeded'. So the index positions in the audit's transcription of (28) are unverified by me. Their physical content is verified.

VERDICT. The identity is a definition plus 2-metric algebra, and it holds with residual 0 under guards that do bite. Not refuted: STANDS.

verifiers.reason:
Every data row holds at source. The alphaXiv quota was exhausted and arxiv.org and NIST are blocked by the proxy, so I read the CODATA 2022 text cached in the scratchpad (d67/src/casmag/all/2409.03787v1.txt, the v1 text of Mohr, Newell, Taylor and Tiesinga). Sec. XIV says 'there is no new relevant input datum for the 2022 adjustment'. Sec. XV.A says 'the 2022 recommended value of G is the same as the 2018 value', from the same 16 inputs with the same expansion factor of 3.9. Table XXXII gives G = 6.674 30(15)e-11 and c = 299 792 458 m/s exact. So value_then = value_now is right for both G and c.

moves_conclusion = 'no' follows. G enters only EXCHANGE_RATE = c^2/(G*LAMBDA) (ledger.py:340, with LAMBDA = 9.982529174194637 from overturn.py:397). No sign statement or verdict that rests on the identity uses G.

The row 'none: a definition plus algebra' is also right. I reran the rederivation and got 24/24 PASS, exit 0. The residuals are symbolic, and there are vacuity guards (C11a to C11c).

The lacked_data answer rests on evidence, not presumption. The identity has no empirical input to have lacked: it was re-derived from scratch, and the one datum near it (G) was checked against a later adjustment and found unchanged. M's hypothesis is therefore tested for this result and finds nothing.

Minor points, none of which moves the grade:
(1) C10 is tautological. The script hard-codes G22 = G18, so it cannot fail on the question of whether G moved. The evidence for that is the READ of CODATA 2022, which I confirmed here.
(2) The tree quotes the exchange rate to 7 significant figures (1.348948e26), which is more precision than G supports. Moving G by one standard uncertainty (1.5e-15) gives 1.348917e26 to 1.348978e26, so the last two digits are not significant. This is a precision note on the tree's use, not a discrepancy with any source, and no conclusion depends on those digits.
(3) There is a citation slip. The 'CODATA 2018' label is at ledger.py:331; foliation.py:580 holds the bare number with no label.
(4) The lacked_data phrase 'each of these reproduces the identity unchanged' is slightly broad for Maeda-Nozawa. Their Lambda-generalised mass is a different function that reduces to the Misner-Sharp mass only at Lambda = 0, though the identity still holds as the definition of m.

Misner & Sharp 1964 itself stays NAMED-NOT-READ, as the audit already says. My note is at /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Claude-Method-Works/6d820e7d-6d3c-5ac7-8067-527dc14c2847/scratchpad/d67/verify/data/misner-sharp-1964.data-lens.txt.

audits.name: Escriva 2025: U = D_t R, Gamma = D_r R, Gamma = sqrt(1 + U^2 - 2M/R), 'generalised Lorentz factor'

source.located: A. Escriva, 'A new approach for simulating PBH formation from generic curvature fluctuations with the Misner-Sharp formalism', arXiv:2504.05813v3 [astro-ph.CO], 28 Nov 2025 (v1 8 Apr 2025). Section 2, p.3-5: eqs. (2.1)-(2.5), (2.12); p.12 (type-II Gamma < 0).
source.via: alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries on 2504.05813. Pages returned: 1-2, 4-5, 11, 13-14, 20-23, 30-32. Eqs. 2.1-2.15 and the p.12 text were read verbatim. Misner & Sharp 1964 (ref [57]), which Escriva cites for the equations, was not read here.

audits.published_statement: p.3-4: 'we need to consider a perfect fluid with the energy-momentum tensor T^{mu nu} = (p + rho) u^mu u^nu + p g^{mu nu} (2.1), and with the following spacetime metric in spherical symmetry: ds^2 = -A(r,t)^2 dt^2 + B(r,t)^2 dr^2 + R(r,t)^2 dOmega^2 (2.2) ... we have chosen zero-shift vector beta^i = 0 (comoving threading) ... u^t = 1/A and u^i = 0 ... (comoving slicing).' '(1/A) dR/dt = D_t R = U(r,t), (1/B) dR/dr = D_r R = Gamma(r,t) (2.3), where D_t and D_r are the proper time and distance derivatives.' 'The Misner-Sharp mass M(r,t) is introduced as M(R) = int_0^R 4 pi Rt^2 rho dRt (2.4), which is related with Gamma, U and R through the constraint: Gamma = sqrt(1 + U^2 - 2M/R) (2.5)'. p.5: 'where Gamma is called the generalised Lorentz factor, which includes the gravitational potential energy and kinetic energy per unit mass.' p.12, same paper: 'we observe the throat-neck structure in the areal radius R, which causes the function Gamma to take negative values'. Also p.12: 'when Gamma < 0, the integrand in Eq. (2.4) (4 pi Rt^2 rho Gamma B), taken over the comoving radial coordinate r includes a locally "negative mass" component'. Units G = c = 1.
published_hypotheses: H1 spherical symmetry, with metric (2.2) diagonal in (t, r)
H2 zero shift beta^i = 0 ('comoving threading'), so that D_t = (1/A) d_t is the derivative along the slice normal
H3 perfect fluid (2.1) and comoving slicing u^t = 1/A (no radial energy flux in these coordinates)
H4 M defined by the integral (2.4) from R = 0, which implies a regular centre; when R is non-monotonic the integral is taken over r with integrand 4 pi R^2 rho Gamma B (p.12)
H5 Einstein field equations: (2.5) is stated as following from them ('Solving the Einstein field equations, the following quantities appear')
H6 implicit in the printed root of (2.5): Gamma >= 0, i.e. R' > 0 with r oriented outward. The same paper departs from this on p.12 (Gamma < 0 for type-II data)

- U without the 1/A factor: residual -(A^2-1) Rdot^2/A^2.
- Gamma without the 1/B factor: residual (B^2-1) R'^2/B^2.
- Sign of M flipped: non-zero.

If the tree's prose 'proper radial length shorter than the areal increment' means magnitudes, that clause is True on the far side. Meanwhile the tree's gamma() returns +sqrt, so gamma() disagrees with the tree's own definition of Gamma beyond a throat. The audit should state the 'dl < dR' clause as holding under the signed reading.

CONCLUSION. The squared identity stands in full generality. The printed positive root, and the chain built on it (Gamma > 1), fails beyond a throat. No computed result of the tree is refuted, because contracts() is equivalent to |Gamma| > 1. The evidence supports NARROWED.

audits.published_statement: p.10: 'In the m = 0 case, the bound simplifies, and actually gives a bound valid for all m >= 0: INT <T00>_w(t,x) g(t)^2 dt >= -(1/16pi^2) INT |g''(t)|^2 dt. (3)' This holds 'for any smooth compactly supported g, and all Hadamard states w' of the Klein-Gordon field in 4-dimensional Minkowski space. The notes that follow say: 'the right-hand side is state-independent. The bound is known not to be optimal. ... remains valid if one take g to be an element of the Sobolev space W^{2,2}(R) ... does not apply to ... discontinuous g.' p.11: 'Suppose that <T00>_w < rho for some interval t in [t0, t0+tau] ... the left-hand side can be minimized over g, to give the minimum eigenvalue of the operator d^4/dt^4 on [t0,t0+tau], with boundary conditions at each end corresponding to vanishing of the function and its first derivative. The upshot is that rho >= -C/tau^4, (4) where the numerical constant C ~ 3.17.' p.13: 'Consider a region between Casimir plates at z = +-L/2 in otherwise flat spacetime and an inertial trajectory parallel to the plates. Let l be the distance ... to the nearest plate ... no experiment conducted along the trajectory in a time interval of less than 2l can possibly know about the existence of the plates ... [as the energy density is supposed constant along the trajectory] (4) gives an a priori bound T00 >= -C/(2l)^4 ~ -3.17/(2l)^4 = -0.20/l^4. By comparison, the known value of the Casimir energy density for the massless minimally coupled scalar field is T00 = -pi^2/(1140 L^4) - (pi^2/(48 L^4))(3 - 2cos^2(pi z/L))/cos^4(pi z/L) which ranges between 3-7% of the bound as z varies in [-L/2, L/2].' p.14: 'There remains an interesting question as to why the Casimir energy density is a comparatively small proportion of the allowed bound.' 2301.01698 p.2 eq.(1.4) gives the same -(1/16pi^2) INT |g''|^2 by Parseval, for the massless field on an inertial worldline, all Hadamard states, and real compactly supported smooth g.
published_hypotheses: P1: free real scalar field with minimal coupling; Eq.(3) holds for every mass m >= 0
P2: four-dimensional Minkowski spacetime with no boundaries
P3: averaging along an inertial worldline (Eq.(15) adds lower-order acceleration terms; 2301.01698 eq.(1.8) covers stationary worldlines)
P4: all Hadamard states; the right-hand side does not depend on the state
P5: g real, smooth and compactly supported; also valid for g in W^{2,2}(R); fails for discontinuous g

P6: Eq.(4) needs <T00> < rho (rho constant) throughout an interval of duration tau at the point, with the sampler in C0^oo of that open interval. The infimum is the least eigenvalue of d^4/dt^4 with clamped ends (footnote 7, Fewster-Teo). C is printed only as 'C ~ 3.17'.
P7: 'The bound is known not to be optimal' (said of Eq.(3); Eq.(4) inherits it)

P8: Casimir a priori bound: plates at z = +-L/2 in otherwise flat spacetime, an inertial trajectory parallel to them, and l the distance to the nearer plate. A causality window (duration < 2l) licenses the Minkowski QEI, following Fewster-Pfenning [31]. The energy density is taken as constant along the trajectory, and the bound applies to all stationary Hadamard states.
P9: the Casimir comparison is for the massless minimally coupled scalar. The passage does not state a boundary condition; the printed form is the Dirichlet one.

audits.name: Bousso covariant entropy bound (lightsheets)

source.located: R. Bousso, 'A Covariant Entropy Conjecture', hep-th/9905177v3 (JHEP 07 (1999) 004) is the primary. It was read alongside: Bousso, 'The holographic principle', hep-th/0203101v2 (RMP 74 (2002) 825); Flanagan-Marolf-Wald, hep-th/9908070v4 (PRD 62 (2000) 084035); Bousso-Casini-Fisher-Maldacena, 1404.5635v2.

audits.published_statement: hep-th/9905177 p.9-10, verbatim: 'Covariant Entropy Conjecture. Let M be a four-dimensional space-time on which Einstein's equation is satisfied with the dominant energy condition holding for matter. Let A be the area of a connected two-dimensional spatial surface B contained in M. Let L be a hypersurface bounded by B and generated by one of the four null congruences orthogonal to B. Let S be the total entropy contained on L. If the expansion of the congruence is non-positive (measured in the direction away from B) at every point on L, then S <= A/4.'  The units are given on p.5: 'We set hbar = c = G = k = 1'. FMW's abstract restates it with units restored as 'S <= A/4G hbar'. On status, review p.19: 'There is no fundamental derivation of the covariant entropy bound ... The resulting entropy bound can be saturated, but no example is known where it is exceeded.'
published_hypotheses: H1: Einstein's equation holds in a four-dimensional spacetime (D dimensions in review Sec. V.E). Source: hep-th/9905177 p.9.

H2: the dominant energy condition holds for matter (1999, p.9; fn.3 suggests causal energy flow may be enough). The review works with the null energy condition plus the causal energy condition, and requires excluding 'unphysical matter content, such as large negative energy' (p.4, Sec. V.D.1).
H3: the spacetime is inextendible and has no naked (null or timelike) singularities (p.9).
H4: L is a NULL hypersurface generated by one of the four null congruences orthogonal to B. Bousso says 'we must use null hypersurfaces' and that the spacelike version fails (p.6; review p.19).
H5: expansion theta <= 0 at every point of L, measured away from B. A generator is terminated where theta would turn positive (caustics), or at a boundary or singularity (pp.10-12).
H6: the geometry is approximately classical and the matter entropy on L can be defined (fluid, or the FMW mode rule). The species problem carries over (review Sec. V.C-V.D).

H7 (status): it is a conjecture. It has been proven only under FMW's classical entropy-current hypotheses, which include the NEC, and for a vacuum-subtracted von Neumann entropy in free fields at weak gravity without the NEC (BCFM 1404.5635).
hypothesis_drift: DROPPED H1/H2/H3/H6: bounds.py:50 and bounds.py:316 carry only the note 'lightsheets', and the canonical hypotheses are only 'light-sheets' and 'A/4G on RHS'. Einstein's equation, the energy condition (DEC in 1999, NEC plus causal in the review), the no-naked-singularity condition and the classical-regime condition are all absent. audits.name: Radial metric of a static spherically symmetric spacetime, g_rr = 1/(1-2m(r)/r)

source.located: Classic textbook form, no single originating paper. Read at source in two arXiv papers that state it exactly: (a) S. A. Hayward, 'Gravitational energy in spherical symmetry', PRD 53, 1938 (1996), arXiv gr-qc/9408002v2, p.4 eq.(4): 'The Misner-Sharp spherically symmetric gravitational energy ... may be defined in units G = 1 by E = (1/2) r (1 - g^{-1}(dr,dr))' ... 'Note that E is an invariant'; p.3: 'The area of a symmetric sphere is 4 pi r^2, so that r is the areal radius'; p.12 eq.(27): '1 - 2E/r = e^{-lambda}(r')^2 - rdot^2, which is the form actually given by Misner & Sharp [4]'. (b) M. Visser, 'Dirty black holes: Entropy versus area', PRD 48, 583 (1993), arXiv hep-th/9303029v2, p.3 eq.(3): 'In any static spherically symmetric asymptotically flat spacetime the metric g_L may without loss of generality be cast into the form ds^2 = -e^{-2phi(r)}(1 - b(r)/r) dt^2 + dr^2/(1 - b(r)/r) + r^2(dtheta^2 + sin^2 theta dphi^2)', with b(infinity) = 2GM and eq.(5) b' = 8 pi G rho r^2.
source.via: alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries on gr-qc/9408002v2 (pp.1-4, 7-10, 12-13, 16-17, 19, 21) and hep-th/9303029v2 (pp.1-17, the whole paper). Misner & Sharp, Phys. Rev. 136, B571 (1964) is NAMED-NOT-READ: it has no arXiv copy, and its form is quoted by Hayward eq.27. Combining (a) with the static diagonal form in (b): g^{rr} = 1/g_rr and E = (r/2)(1 - g^{rr}) give g_rr = 1/(1 - 2m/r) with m = E. Re-derived symbolically (C1a).

audits.published_statement: Hayward gr-qc/9408002 eq.(4): 'E = (1/2) r (1 - g^{-1}(dr,dr))' in units G = 1, 'an invariant', where r is the areal radius (area 4 pi r^2). Prop.1: a sphere is trapped iff E > r/2, marginal iff E = r/2, untrapped iff E < r/2. p.8: 'E may be negative, as in the negative-energy Schwarzschild solution'. Prop.6: 'If the dominant energy condition holds on an untrapped spatial hypersurface with regular centre, then E >= 0'. Visser hep-th/9303029 eq.(3): 'In any static spherically symmetric asymptotically flat spacetime the metric may without loss of generality be cast into the form ds^2 = -e^{-2phi}(1 - b/r)dt^2 + dr^2/(1 - b/r) + r^2 dOmega^2'; eq.(5): b' = 8 pi G rho r^2; 'This metric has putative horizons at values of r satisfying b(r_H) = r_H.' With b = 2m (G = 1) this is the tree's radial part dr^2/(1 - 2m(r)/r), and the proper radial length on a t = const slice is dl = dr/sqrt(1 - 2m/r).
published_hypotheses: Spherical symmetry: a warped product with round spheres of area 4 pi r^2, r the areal radius (Hayward p.2-3).
Static: a hypersurface-orthogonal timelike Killing vector, so the metric is diagonal in (t, r) and the t = const slices are orthogonal to the Killing vector (Visser eq.3).
r usable as a coordinate: dr != 0, i.e. away from marginal spheres where 2m = r (Visser: 'putative horizons at b(r_H) = r_H'). In the static region 1 - 2m/r > 0.
Asymptotic flatness (Visser eq.3). It is used only to set phi(infinity) = 0 and identify b(infinity) = 2GM, not for the local form of g_rr.
Units: G = 1 (Hayward); c = 1 (Visser keeps G explicit, b = 2Gm).

No energy condition is needed for the definition. E < 0 is explicitly allowed (negative-energy Schwarzschild); E >= 0 follows only under the dominant energy condition plus an untrapped slice with a regular centre (Hayward Prop.6).
hypothesis_drift: ADDED, UNNAMED (a wording discrepancy, not a narrowing): overturn.py:79 and 92-94, and the L3 header at :401, call the L3 measurement 'ansatz-free: no Phi, no Plummer, no shell, just the areal radius and the Misner-Sharp mass'. audits.lacked_data: In June 2012, three weeks before the discovery, the authors had no Higgs boson and no coupling data. Later data confirm kappa = 1 for W and Z (about 5%) and for t, b and tau (7-12%), and the muon is emerging. For the statement as published, the new data change nothing: nothing contradicts it and the re-derivation agrees. For the payload's fermions e, u and d, the missing data are STILL missing. kappa_e is bounded only to below 262, and kappa_e = 0 is not excluded. kappa_u and kappa_d are assumed, not measured. So M's hypothesis holds in a narrow sense. The 2012 statement is not wrong. But the tree's 'm_e is 100% Higgs, subtract exactly 1' (address.py:514) and 'what the Higgs gives the fermions' (excite.py:145-147) rest on an SM prediction for exactly the particles no experiment has tested yet. Against over-reading this: every Yukawa that has been measured agrees with kappa = 1, and a large kappa_e needs fine-tuned cancellation (2501.07628 p.5). For caution: 2501.07628 exhibits models consistent with all current data that have kappa_e around 265-925. Two tree results move: K_mu, one-for-one with kappa_e, and the H2 stable-matter f, in proportion to kappa_l. Three do not move: C5, D27 and C2.

(i) The renormalisable-SM relation kappa_f = 1 for e, u and d is asserted as fact at excite.py:145-147 and address.py:514. Check C proves kappa_f = d ln m_f/d ln phi, and the data bound kappa_e only to below 262 (computed from ATLAS 1909.10235) while assuming kappa_u and kappa_d (2207.00092 p.8). (ii) The single-doublet premise behind massform.py:212 is never named. The tree's own H-TREE correctly adds tree level. The uses that need only m(0) = 0 (C5, D27, C2) survive any single-doublet mass function (check D). The linear uses (K_mu, D20 for an electron-borne source, the S part of f) hold only on the smaller class kappa = 1, which is untested for the payload's fermions. The grade is not DATA-DEPENDENT because none of these kappas has moved or is contested; they are unmeasured.
audits.what_would_change_the_grade: The grade would become STANDS if the tree named an H-SM hypothesis at excite.py:145-147 and address.py:514 and carried it into K_mu and f. H-SM here means one doublet with kappa_e = kappa_u = kappa_d = 1, bounded only to |kappa_e| < 262 and assumed for u and d. It would also become STANDS if measurements (for example the FCC-ee Higgs pole run, projected at 1.6 times y_SM, or light-quark Yukawa probes) found these kappas consistent with 1. It would become DATA-DEPENDENT if a measured or contested kappa_e or kappa_l came out different from 1; then K_mu and the H2 stable-matter density move (checks G2 and G3). It would become WRONG only if a non-SM kappa were measured for a payload fermion while the tree kept asserting 'exactly 1'. Nothing of that kind exists.

verifiers.lens: REFUTE THE GRADE (either direction) for 1206.2942-phi: the audit grades it NARROWED
verifiers.reason:
I tried to refute the grade in both directions and could not. The grade NARROWED holds.

THE SOURCE, read myself. I read 1206.2942v1 through alphaXiv. The p.4 sentence is verbatim: "Note that (in unitary gauge) the masses of the W± and Z0 weak vector bosons and the fermions are proportional to φ". It is framed as "The transition ... in the SM", with eq. (1) defining φ/√2 ≡ <H0>. Three more points check out: p.8 says the one-loop effective-potential vev is gauge-dependent; eq. (20) on p.9 uses v(0) = 174 GeV, so the paper does use two normalisations; and the paper is dated 13 Jun 2012. The tree sites say what the audit says they say:
- excite.py:144-147: "which is what the Higgs gives the fermions and W, Z", with no SM, single-doublet or kappa hypothesis named.
- address.py:513-514: "m_e is 100% Higgs, so subtract exactly 1". This is used through excite.py:971-974 (K_mu_rows).
- massform.py:208-214: names H-TREE but no single-doublet premise.

AGAINST NARROWED, TOWARD STANDS. The source says "in the SM", and the electron is an SM fermion, so one could say the tree uses the result inside its stated scope. But the tree asserts that scope as a fact about the real electron, u and d. It never carries it as a named hypothesis.
- The data do not test that fact. I read 1909.10235 pp.1-2 and 7: BR(H→ee) < 3.6e-4 observed, the SM value is ≈5e-9, the best fit is (0.0±1.8)e-4, and the paper says there is "no evidence of Higgs boson decays into first- or second-generation quarks or leptons".
- I recomputed both numbers independently: BR_SM = 5.225e-9, and |kappa_e| < 262.5. Including the width feedback only moves this to 262.54. kappa_e = 0 is not excluded.
- I read 2207.00092 p.8 verbatim: "SM values are assumed for the coupling strength modifiers of first-generation fermions".
- So 'exactly 1' for the payload's fermions rests on an untested SM prediction that the tree does not name. That is a hypothesis drop, not a scope match, so STANDS is not supported.

AGAINST NARROWED, TOWARD DATA-DEPENDENT or WRONG. No measured or contested kappa for e, u or d differs from 1. In this docket's own usage, DATA-DEPENDENT means the result turns on contested or variant data (for example top-mass definitions), and unmeasured is not contested. WRONG has no support: the statement is re-derived. I ran the auditor's script: 29 PASS, exit 0. The linear-use arithmetic also reproduces: K_mu(H1, kappa_e=0) = +0.2689 against the tree's -0.7311, with dK_mu/dkappa_e = -1.

DISCREPANCIES FOUND. They are recorded, and none of them moves the grade.
1. The sign of check H's QED estimate is off. The script gives d ln m_e/d ln v ≈ 1/(1-γ_m) = 1.0035. With the standard dm/dlnμ = -γ_m m, the condition m(m)^(1+γ) ∝ v gives 1/(1+γ_m) = 0.9965. The size of the correction (3.5e-3) is the same, and the check is labelled ESTIMATE.
2. 2501.07628's κ_e,max values (265 in the text, 266/925/323 in Tab. 13) come from a χ² that includes an "optimistic FCC-ee projection" factor of 17.8 on the Bhabha bound (eq. 78) and HL-LHC direct-search masses. The audit describes them as "consistent with current data". That wording is loose, but in the conservative direction: a model that survives the projected constraints also survives the current ones.
3. A refinement that makes the narrowing stronger, not weaker. Check C's identity, kappa_f = d ln m_f/d ln φ, holds only when h enters through φ = v + h, that is a single-doublet linear realisation (SMEFT). In a 2HDM or HEFT the measured hff coupling is not the static-background derivative the tree needs. This adds weight to the single-doublet drift the audit already names.

Other values the audit cites also check out: λ_C,e/λ_h = 2.45e5, the ATLAS κ_V and κ_F values, |κ_c| < 5.7, and H→μμ at 2.0σ.

verifiers.lens: RE-RUN THE RE-DERIVATION (encoding check + vacuity guard) for 1206.2942-phi
verifiers.reason:
I copied the script to verify/rederive/phi_copy.py and re-ran it: 29 PASS, 0 failures, exit 0, about 1 s of CPU. The audit's report is reproduced exactly: v = 246.219651 GeV, SM BR(H->ee) = 5.225e-9, |kappa_e| < 262, K_mu(H1) = -0.73111.

ENCODING. Part A is the published statement at tree level, not a toy of it. With explicit Pauli matrices, |D_mu H|^2 for H = (0, phi/sqrt2) with Y = 1/2 gives m_W = g phi/2 and m_Z = sqrt(g^2+g'^2) phi/2, and the photon combination is massless. For fermions, m_f = y phi/sqrt2 is typed in rather than derived from the Yukawa operator. That step is trivial, but "re-derived" is strictly true only for W and Z.

I checked the G block against the tree itself. Importing address.py read-only gives dln_lambda_dln_v() = 2/9, K_mu(0.06, H1) = -0.7311111 and K_mu(0.06, H2) = -0.94, so the script's f_H1 matches the tree's code and not just its prose.

At source, 2501.07628 eqs (5), (6) and (10) match the script's m(phi) = phi/sqrt2 (y - C phi^2/2) and kappa_e = 1 - v^3 C/(sqrt2 m_e) exactly.

VACUITY GUARD (1206.2942-phi/vacuity_phi.py, output in vacuity_phi.out). The substantive checks bite when their hypotheses are negated:
- A3 fails with Y = -1/2, and fails with the vev placed in the Q = +1 component.
- A4 fails for m ~ phi^2 and for m = y phi + u.
- A5/D1 fails for a 2HDM with a second vev: m(0) = y2 u/sqrt2.
- D1 fails for HEFT with generic a, b: m(0) = -(v y/sqrt2)(a - b - 1).
- D2 oddness fails for the Weinberg operator, although m(0) = 0 still holds there.
- B1 fails for a non-unitary 2U.
- E1 fails for an offset source mass m0 phi/v + c.

Four checks are tautological and would pass whatever the inputs:
- C1 is the definition kappa = m'(v) v/m(v) = d ln m/d ln phi at v. It also passes for an arbitrary m = phi^7 + 3 phi^2 + 1.
- G2 and G3 test the script's own model (f_H2 = kl*S), not tree code.
- H1 is one-sided, so a correction of the opposite sign also passes. This one is labelled ESTIMATE, as it should be.
- F4 is robust: |kappa_e| < 249-262 for m_H between 125.0 and 125.2 GeV and Gamma_H between 3.7 and 4.1 MeV.

TWO NARROWINGS OF THE AUDIT'S OWN WORDING. Neither moves the grade.
(1) Check D shows the single-doublet contrapositive "m_f > 0 implies phi != 0" holds for operators that are analytic in H (SMEFT). The audit says "any gauge-invariant operators", which is too broad. In HEFT, m(h) is a free function with no symmetric point, and m(0) = 0 is not forced. So H-SMEFT/analyticity is a further unnamed hypothesis beside the single doublet.
(2) The audit says check C "proves kappa_f = d ln m_f/d ln phi at v for any m_f(phi)". That holds only with a canonical Higgs kinetic term. 2501.07628 eq. (7), READ, carries a factor (1 + v^2 C_phi,kin) from O_phi-box and O_phiD. So the measured kappa_e bounds g_hee, and d ln m_e/d ln phi = kappa_e/(1 + v^2 C_phi,kin). That correction is O(v^2/Lambda^2) and universal, which is negligible against the window of 262.

VERDICT. The re-derivation is genuine, re-runs cleanly, and is not vacuous where it matters. The data numbers reproduce. The grade NARROWED is supported for the reasons the audit gives: the tree asserts kappa = 1 for e, u and d as fact at excite.py:145-147 and address.py:514, and it never names the single-doublet premise. The grade is not refuted.

verifiers.lens: THE DATA CLAIM: every data_at_publication row and the lacked_data answer, checked at source; does moves_conclusion follow; is M's hypothesis answered with evidence
verifiers.reason:
I checked the data rows at source and nearly all of them stand. I found one error that needs fixing, and it over-represents in M's favour. I also found three precision slips. None of the four moves the grade.

CONFIRMED AT SOURCE
- 1206.2942v1 is dated 13 Jun 2012. The p.4 sentence is verbatim, unitary-gauge parenthetical included. v(0)=174 GeV appears at eq.(20), p.9. The gauge-dependence warning is on p.8.
- 1909.10235: BR(H->ee) < 3.6e-4 observed (3.5e-4 expected), pp.1 and 7. The SM formula G_F m_H m_e^2/(4 sqrt2 pi Gamma_H) ~ 5e-9 is on p.2. Gamma_H = 4.1 MeV is on p.5. p.2 says "no evidence of Higgs boson decays into first- or second-generation quarks or leptons". Recomputed: BR_SM = 5.2249e-9, so |kappa_e| < 262.5. Feedback from the width is 0.035% of Gamma_H, which is negligible.
- 2207.00092: m_H = 125.09 (p.2). kappa_V = 1.035 +- 0.031 and kappa_F = 0.95 +- 0.05 (p.8). H->mumu at 2.0 sigma (p.7). kappa_c < 5.7 (p.9). p.8 says "SM values are assumed for the coupling strength modifiers of first-generation fermions". p.13 gives t, b, tau at 7-12% and W, Z at about 5%.
- 2602.08512: |kappa_c| < 3.5 (p.3). p.1 says light-quark Yukawas "remain largely unconstrained".
- 2501.07628: eq.(10) is exact. The figures 260, 120 and 1.6 are on pp.2-3. The fine-tuning remark is on p.5.
- CODATA 2022 Table XXXIII: m_e = 0.51099895069(16) MeV and G_F = 1.1663787(6)e-5, giving v = 246.219651 GeV.
- FLAG 2024 Table 12 and eq.(43): m_u = 2.14(8) MeV and m_d = 4.70(5) MeV.
- moves_conclusion: address.py:514 is literally dln_mp_dln_v - 1, so K_mu moves one-for-one with kappa_e. The script exits 0, and K_mu(H1) is -0.7311 at kappa_e = 1 and +0.2689 at kappa_e = 0. Under H2, f = kappa_l S. The YES/NO split follows from these.
- M's hypothesis is answered with evidence, not presumed. In June 2012 there were no couplings. Now every measured coupling agrees with kappa = 1. The payload species e, u and d are still unmeasured: kappa_e = 0 is not excluded, and kappa_u and kappa_d are assumed.

ERROR (must be corrected; it over-represents in M's favour)
- lacked_data says "2501.07628 exhibits models consistent with all current data that have kappa_e around 265-925". later_literature repeats the claim ("while staying consistent with current data").
- The source does not say this. The Table 13 maxima (266, 925 and 323) come from fits to PROJECTED constraints. Sec.3.4 says "We will now consider constraints from higher energy runs of the FCC-ee". Table 12 gives projected FCC-ee 240 GeV uncertainties. The EW fit sets the observables to their SM values with rescaled errors (p.25). The Bhabha term carries an FCC-ee factor of 17.8 (p.23). Table 10 uses HL-LHC projections for direct searches.
- The current ATLAS h->ee bound is not in those fits. The paper calls 265 only "comparable" to it (p.24).
- kappa_e = 925 is excluded by current data, by the very bound of 262 that this audit computes.
- Correct reading: these models leave kappa_e unconstrained up to about 265-925 by every probe other than the direct h->ee search and a Higgs-pole run. Today's allowed range is |kappa_e| < ~262.

What came later: Pound-Rebka-Snider (1%), Gravity Probe A (2e-4), the Galileo satellites (about 1e-5) and cm-scale lab clocks (2207.07145) all confirm Z = Delta U/c^2. The G measurements spread by 5.5e-4, but CODATA 2022 leaves G unchanged. Does any of it change the conclusion? No, and the evidence runs both ways. The coefficients 2 pi and (2/3) pi are pure mathematics given inverse-square gravity and uniform density, so no datum enters them. G moves R* by at most 2.8e-4. What the Newtonian reading leaves out (pressure, O(x^2) GR terms, LPI violation) was computed here at 3.3e-19, about 1e-18 and under 1e-5. The redshift was later measured in the tree's own regime (cm, 1e-18) and agreed, though in an exterior field, so the interior step remains a theorem rather than a measurement. (2) Independent re-derivation (verify/refute/usp_convention.py).
- Phi = -GM(3R^2 - r^2)/(2R^3) is C^1-matched to -GM/r at R.

(a) The claim 'the exact GR ratio is 3*sqrt(1-x), not 3' holds in one convention only. That convention normalises the fractional shift to the reference (twin) clock: 1 - s0/s_ref. If the shift is normalised to the courier's own clock, Z = s_ref/s0 - 1 with s0 = sqrt(A(0)), then the deficit ratio is EXACTLY 3 for every x < 8/9 (sympy). The 'what_would_change_the_grade' clause, 'for a compact source the ratio is 3sqrt(1-2GM/(Rc^2))', inherits this convention dependence.
(b) The crossover factor 'sqrt(3)(1-x)^(1/4)' is evaluated at a single x. That is not the crossover ratio, because the two crossovers sit at different R. Solving Z_inf(R1) = eps and Z_srf(R2) = eps properly gives R2/R1 = sqrt(3)(1 - 4eps/3 + ...) in BOTH conventions (verify/refute/usp_crossover.py). The axiomatic form is Minguzzi arXiv:1709.06494v4 (Rev. Math. Phys. 31, 1930001 (2019)): p.11 Def. 2.1-2.2, Example 2.1, and p.87 sec. 3.1 (polar cone, (C^o)^o = C).

audits.published_statement: 2009.08834 pp.12-13: 'vectors u, v in C+ in the positive causal cone C+ = {v = (v_t, v_x) in R x R^n | <v,v> >= 0, v_t > 0} of the standard Minkowski space ... satisfy the reversed triangle inequality (6.1) |u + v| >= |u| + |v| as well as the reversed Cauchy-Schwarz inequality <u,v> >= |u||v|, see e.g. [O'N83, Prop. 5.30].' Closure under addition follows directly: (u+v)_t > 0 and <u+v,u+v> = |u|^2+|v|^2+2<u,v> >= 0. 1709.06494 p.11: 'All our cones will be closed and convex'. Example 2.1 there: the causal cones C_x = {y in T_xM\{0} : g(y,y) <= 0, y future directed} of a time-oriented Lorentzian manifold form a cone structure, so the Lorentzian causal cone is admitted as a closed, sharp, convex cone.

The cone as the sources define it excludes the origin (v_t > 0; 1709.06494 p.11).
Any finite dimension n+1 >= 2.
A round (quadratic) cone. Beyond the round case Minguzzi takes convexity as a defining property of every admitted cone rather than deriving it.

audits.published_statement: p.10 (after Eq. 3.12): 'The noise kernel is defined in terms of the unrenormalized stress-tensor operator T_ab[g;x) on a given background metric g_ab, thus a regulator is implicitly assumed on the right-hand side of Eq. (3.11). However, for a linear quantum field the above kernel - the expectation function of a bi-tensor - is free of ultraviolet divergences because the regularized T_ab[g;x) differs from the renormalized T^R_ab[g;x) by the identity operator times some tensor counterterms, see Eq. (3.6), so that in the subtraction (3.12) the counterterms cancel. Consequently the ultraviolet behavior of <T_ab(x) T_cd(y)> is the same as that of <T_ab(x)><T_cd(y)>, and T_ab can be replaced by the renormalized operator T^R_ab in Eq. (3.11); an alternative proof of this result is given in Ref. [7, 8]. The noise kernel should be thought of as a distribution function, the limit of coincidence points has meaning only in the sense of distributions.' Sec. 5.2.1 p.29: 'the noise kernel is finite for y != x ... When the coincidence limit is taken divergences do occur.' p.25: Phillips-Hu's expression 'holds for x != y without recourse to renormalization of the Green function, showing that N(x,y) is always finite for x != y (and off the light cone for massless theories).'
published_hypotheses: H-lin: a LINEAR (free) quantum field (p.10, 'for a linear quantum field'; the scalar field with coupling xi, Eqs. (3.4)-(3.5)).

H-ct: the regularized and renormalized stress operators differ by a c-number, T^R_ab = T_ab + F^C_ab * I, where F^C are local functionals of the metric that depend on the regulator (Eq. 3.6, p.8). This is true for a linear field. It is not true for interacting fields, where the composite-operator counterterms are operators.
H-had: physically acceptable (Hadamard) states, for which <psi|T^R_ab|phi> is finite (p.8).

H-sep: the finiteness statement is for separated points x != y (and off the light cone for massless fields, p.25). At coincidence the kernel has meaning 'only in the sense of distributions' (p.10), and pointwise 'divergences do occur' (p.29).
H-reg: a regulator is implicit (dimensional regularization in Secs. 3-4, point separation in Sec. 5).
H-qf, needed only by the ALTERNATIVE route of Sec. 5.2.1 and not by the Sec. 3.2 argument: a free field in a state that obeys Wick's theorem (quasi-free), Eqs. (5.20)-(5.21).

A (THEOREM, exact sympy, generic 3x3 Hermitian operators in a generic Hermitian state): under A -> A + L*1, with L a symbolic counterterm that may diverge with the regulator, the covariance <{t_A,t_B}>/2 and the fluctuation operator t_A = A - <A> are unchanged, and the mean moves by exactly L. This is the whole Sec. 3.2 argument, and it holds in any state. B (THEOREM, exact sympy Wick contraction with ordered Wightman symbols, G(a,b) != G(b,a)): H&V Eq. (5.19) reduces to Eq. (5.21), with every disconnected pairing cancelling, including every G(x,x') and G(y,y'). At x'=x, y'=y it gives Eq. (5.22), G = 2(G_xy^2 + G_yx^2). H&V's formulas are re-derived with no discrepancy. B' (NUMERIC, 2-mode truncated Fock space): Wick's 4-point formula holds in the vacuum to 1.6e-16 and fails in a one-particle state (relative error 0.82). So the Sec. 5.2.1 route needs a quasi-free state and the Sec. 3.2 route does not. C (ILLUSTRATION): in flat space for a massless field, G^2 -> infinity as y -> x, the pointwise divergence H&V describe in 5.2.1. D (ILLUSTRATION, flat massless 4D, worldline energy density C = 3/(2 pi^4 (tau - i eps)^8), Ford-Roman Eq. 53): mpmath quadrature of the Lorentzian-smeared variance matches the contour value 3/(2 pi^4 (a+eps)^8) to better than 1e-8 at eps = 0.3, 0.1 and 0.03. The curved-worldline pull-back (Fewster 1208.5399 Sec. 3.3) is not run here and stays NAMED.

later_literature.ref: Ford & Roman, 'Minkowski Vacuum Stress Tensor Fluctuations', gr-qc/0506026 (PRD 2005)
later_literature.what: Flat space, massless, 4D. The stress-tensor correlation function diverges as (x-x')^-8 but is a well-defined distribution, and non-time-ordered correlators 'have no pole term and are hence finite in dimensional regularization' (Sec. III A); this agrees with H&V. Averaging along a worldline (time only) gives a finite variance, Eq. 49, 3/(2 pi^4 a^8). Averaging over space only DIVERGES, Eq. 50, ~ 1/(pi^{7/2} a b^7), so the no-new-renormalisation conclusion for a smeared variance needs TIME smearing. They also caution (Sec. III C) that setting r = 0 before averaging, versus taking the full spacetime limit, 'needs to be studied more carefully'. That is the gap Fewster's wavefront argument closes.

later_literature.ref: Perez & Sudarsky, 'Renormalization of the Quantum Stress Tensor Fluctuations and the Limits of Semiclassical Gravity', arXiv 2512.17789v2 (Jan 2026)
later_literature.what: For the POINTWISE coincident fluctuation <T_ab(x)T_cd(x)> they state that 'subtracting a state-independent divergent quantity is no longer sufficient'. They renormalize the quartic composite with the Hollands-Wald OPE (free scalar, Hadamard states) and argue that its ambiguities 'appear not to exceed' those of <T_ab> and 'should cancel' in Delta(T T). Their prescription sets the Minkowski-vacuum pointwise fluctuations to zero, while the time-smeared vacuum variance (Ford-Roman; check D) is strictly positive, so the pointwise-renormalized and smeared variances are different objects. The paper does NOT contradict H&V 3.2, which is about separated points and distributions, nor the tree's smeared claim. It confirms that 'no NEW renormalisation' is false for the pointwise variance, so the flag must be read as applying to the smeared variance only.

audits.lacked_data: This result is structural: it rests on the operator algebra of a linear field and on the form of the renormalization counterterm (Eq. 3.6). It takes no numerical input. What the authors did not have in 2008: (i) a rigorous pull-back to a worldline in curved spacetime (Fewster 1208.5399, 2012); (ii) an OPE renormalization of the pointwise quartic fluctuation (the Hollands-Wald OPE, 2312.01096, as applied by Perez-Sudarsky 2512.17789 in 2025/26). Neither changes the Sec. 3.2 conclusion. (i) extends it to the case smeared along a curve; that step is named, not run, here. (ii) concerns the coincident pointwise object that H&V themselves said diverges (p.29). Evidence against M's hypothesis for THIS result: the re-derivation (checks A and B) reproduces H&V's argument and their Eqs. (5.21)-(5.22) exactly, and two independent papers, from 2005 and 2026, agree with it on the class it states. Evidence of a limitation: the tree's flag covers a broader class than H&V's (smeared, integrating over the diagonal), and the extra piece does not come from H&V.
audits.grade_evidence: The SOURCE holds on the class it states. It was READ at p.10. (5.21)-(5.22) with no discrepancy (checks B1-B3). No datum enters. What is narrowed is the tree's USE. CURVED_VARIANCE_NEEDS_QUARTIC_RENORMALISATION = False at noise.py:274, and the D22 text at ledger.py:586-588 and 1920-1922, concern the worldline-smeared curved variance and carry the status 'H&V 3.2, READ'. For the TIME-smeared variance on a curve to need no new renormalisation, the wavefront pull-back (Fewster 1208.5399 Sec. 3.3) is also required; the tree marks it NAMED, NOT RUN, and it is not run here either. verifiers.reason:
RE-RUN: I copied the script to verify/rederive/ and ran it. All 14 checks pass with exit 0 in about 10 s, and the numbers match the audit: the Wick error is 1.59e-16 in the vacuum and 0.818 in the one-particle state, the D quadrature agrees with the closed form at eps = 0.3, 0.1 and 0.03, and the limit is 0.015398973.

WHAT THE SCRIPT ENCODES. Check A works on 3x3 matrices, which looks like a toy, but the Sec. 3.2 argument is purely algebraic: a c-number shift cancels in t = T - <T>. The generic symbolic Hermitian operators and state encode that argument exactly, so A is the theorem's actual content and not a stand-in. A does have a limit in reach. It proves the counterterm cancels; it does not prove that the remaining <T^R T^R> is finite in a general Hadamard state. B proves finiteness only for quasi-free states (the disconnected pairings cancel and no G(x,x') survives). So for a Hadamard state that is not quasi-free, finiteness at separated points rests on H&V's assertion (H-had) and is not re-derived here. This tightens the wording of B'2 ("route A does not need quasi-free" is true of the cancellation, not of finiteness). It does not change the grade, because the tree cites only the cancellation as READ. B is a faithful symbolic re-derivation of Eqs. (5.19)->(5.21)->(5.22) with ordered Wightman symbols. C is a trivial illustration. D is a flat-space illustration, and its convention matches Ford-Roman exactly: I READ gr-qc/0506026v3 pp.11-13 through alphaXiv. Their Eq. (40) uses int dtau g_L(a,tau) C with a = 2*alpha, which is the script's convention, Eq. (49) is 3/(2 pi^4 a^8), Eq. (50) is the divergence when smearing over space only, and Eq. (53) is C = 3/(2 pi^4 (t-t')^8). One difference: the script adds a Wightman -i*eps that Eq. (53) does not print. That is standard and is consistent with FR's integration-by-parts definition.

VACUITY GUARDS (verify/rederive/vacuity.py). Every check fails when its hypothesis is negated.
- V1, H-ct negated: with an operator counterterm L*C in place of L*1, the covariance shifts by an amount linear in L (numerically -5839L/30276).
- V2, raw moment: without the subtraction, the raw second moment is not shift-invariant.
- V3, wrong disconnected-subtraction factor: B1 fails with factor 0 or 1 and passes only with 2.
- V3b, non-Wick state: adding a connected 4-point cumulant makes B1 fail.
- V4, time smearing negated: the pointwise value grows like eps^-8, and smearing along a spatial line grows like eps^-7 (eps^7 times the value converges to 0.00481). This reproduces FR Eq. (50)'s conclusion that the time smearing is what makes the variance finite.
So no check passes vacuously.

TREE CITATIONS. noise.py:198-213 and 274-275 are verbatim as quoted. The D22 text in ledger.py has moved: the audit cites ledger.py:1917-1923 and 1920-1922, but the text is now at ledger.py:1974-1981 (the 'NEW renormalisation (Hu & Verdaguer 3.2, READ)' line is 1978). ledger.py:584-589 is correct. NAMED'). That supports the audit's 'no hidden false claim'.

(52), the Lorentzian worldline function C(t0,0), evaluates at t0 = 0 to 1/(pi^4 a^8), which is 2/3 of Eq. (41) at r = 0 and of Eq. (49), both 3/(2 pi^4 a^8). audits.name: No-communication (no-signalling) theorem

source.located: Classics: P. H. Eberhard, Nuovo Cimento B 46, 392 (1978), and Ghirardi, Rimini & Weber, Lett. Nuovo Cimento 27, 293 (1980). Neither has an arXiv copy. Read through exact restatements: G. C. Ghirardi, arXiv:1305.2305 (2013), sec. 4 eq.(12), pp.13-14, which is the GRW proof restated by its first author; and Peres & Terno, Rev. Mod. Phys. 76, 93 (2004), arXiv:quant-ph/0212023, sec. II.E eqs.(9)-(11), pp.8-9.
source.via: alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries on 1305.2305 and quant-ph/0212023. Eberhard 1978 and GRW 1980 themselves are NAMED-NOT-READ: only their restatements were read. The tree cites no source for the theorem; it only names it (transit.py:318, ledger.py:452 and 605).

audits.published_statement: Peres-Terno (quant-ph/0212023 pp.8-9): a sufficient condition for 'no instantaneous information transfer' from a distant intervention is [A_mu_m, B_nu_n] = 0 (eq.9), where A and B are Alice's and Bob's Kraus matrices. Bob's probability 'irrespective of what Alice found', p_nu = sum_mu tr(sum B A rho A^+ B^+) (eq.10), reduces through sum_mu E_mu = 1 to p_nu = tr(sum_n B rho B^+) (eq.11), 'whence all expressions involving Alice's operators have totally disappeared.' Ghirardi 2013 (1305.2305 p.13, eq.12): under no action, a unitary evolution, or an ideal or non-ideal NONSELECTIVE measurement on S(2), 'the reduced statistical operator of subsystem S(1) does not change in any way whatsoever.' p.14: under SELECTIVE measurements the distant physics 'is actually changed', but the change depends on the outcome, and using it needs 'subluminal communication'.
published_hypotheses: H1 Linear quantum mechanics: operations are linear, completely positive Kraus maps rho -> sum A rho A^+ (Peres-Terno eq.6), with Born-rule probabilities.

H2 The intervention is NON-SELECTIVE, i.e. trace-preserving and summed over Alice's outcomes (sum_mu E_mu = 1; Peres-Terno eq.10->11, Ghirardi eq.12). A selective update does change the distant conditional state (Ghirardi p.14).
H3 The operations are local: Alice's and Bob's Kraus operators commute (Peres-Terno eq.9, stated as SUFFICIENT). In finite dimensions this is the tensor product H_A (x) H_B with A (x) I.
H4 There are no closed causal loops (Peres-Terno p.9: 'we assume that there are no closed causal loops').

H5 The content is non-relativistic (Peres-Terno sec. III.D: 'Replace superluminal by supersonic and the argument is exactly the same'). The speed of any actual signal is set by the carrier's dynamics (sec. III.C). The theorem forbids signalling BY the entanglement; it does not itself set c.
hypothesis_drift: WEAKENED WORDING (H2), transit.py:17-18 and :176, 'invariant ... under EVERY operation A can perform': the theorem covers every NON-SELECTIVE local operation. A selective (post-selected) operation moves B's conditional state; check C4a gives rho_B -> |0><0|. The file's own teleportation step relies on exactly this, so the omission is in the wording, not in the physics.

INSTRUMENT SAMPLES LESS THAN IT CLAIMS, transit.py:97-110: only U (x) I on one Bell pair is sampled (6 draws with seed 7, 40 draws with seed 101). Measurements, ancillas and general CPTP maps are never sampled. Closed by this audit: C1 proves the identity for generic symbolic Kraus sets, and C3 samples 1,200 random CPTP-with-ancilla and non-selective operations, worst deviation 9.99e-16. This is a gap in the instrument, not a narrowing of the theorem.

THEOREM ASSERTED, NOT DERIVED, transit.py:149 and :318: READING_CARRIES_NOTHING_ALONE = True is a hard-coded constant, and the selftest checks that constant against True. The instrument measures one instance; C1 supplies the missing derivation.

DROPPED H1 (linearity), at ledger.py:451-453 (D13), ledger.py:604-605 (D23), index3.py:1366 and axis.py:208-210 ('provably ... because the no-communication theorem is a theorem'): 'proved' holds only for linear, completely positive dynamics. Gisin / Simon-Buzek-Gisin (restated in 2412.20854) show that a nonlinear local map signals, and C4d exhibits one: Bob's state moves by 0.0950. The tree never names linearity as a hypothesis.

DROPPED H3 (commuting local operations / tensor-product subsystems), D13 'closes the entangled variant': Sorkin 1993 shows that microcausality alone does not exclude signalling once non-local ideal measurements are allowed; C4b reproduces his numbers. Fewster-Verch exclude this by ADDING the Time-Slice axiom (2307.08524). Donnelly-Giddings (1607.01025) show local commuting subalgebras cannot be defined in perturbative gravity. Neither paper exhibits signalling; both show the hypothesis is not automatic.
DROPPED H4 (no closed causal loops), D13/D23: Peres-Terno assume it on p.9, yet the same ledger carries a CTC row (O3) beside D13/D23 in the specthm R11 status line. H4 is not named.

NOT DRIFT (correct use of H5): D13 keeps the classical-carrier limb ('<= c IN THE METRIC ITS CARRIER PROPAGATES IN') separate from the entangled limb, as Peres-Terno sec. III.C-D do. D23 correctly calls the zero advantage 'ZERO BY CONSTRUCTION' (ledger.py:600-603).

audits.lacked_data: M's hypothesis tested for this result. What the 1978/1980 authors had was finite-dimensional linear QM with Kraus operations. The theorem is an algebraic identity with no empirical input, so no later measurement can move it inside its hypotheses; C1 re-derives it exactly. Three things came later. (i) Sorkin 1993 found the weak point in the measurement model for QFT regions, not in the identity. Fewster-Verch closed it by adding axioms, without overturning the theorem. (ii) Gisin / Simon-Buzek-Gisin showed linearity is necessary, and experiment now bounds one class of nonlinearity at |eps_gamma| < 4.7e-11, consistent with zero. (iii) Donnelly-Giddings showed that the commuting-subsystem structure the theorem assumes cannot be defined in perturbative gravity. Evidence either way: nothing read here shows entanglement signalling in linear QM with local non-selective operations. Nothing here shows that H1, H3 and H4 hold in the gravitational or CTC settings the board also considers. So missing data does not change the conclusion within the class. It matters only at the class boundary, and those limits must be named as hypotheses, not treated as refutations.
audits.grade_evidence: In its published class the theorem stands and is re-derived exactly: C1 (sympy identity for generic Kraus sets), C2 (every angle of transit.py's U) and C3 (1,200 random CPTP operations, worst 9.99e-16). No datum enters it: C6 shows D23's advantage is 0 by construction at every distance. The tree's own uses in transit.py and D23 sit inside that class. The grade is NARROWED, not WRONG, and it is not a finding against the tree's transit conclusion. It is NARROWED because the tree states the theorem with hypotheses dropped. Non-selectivity is missing from 'EVERY operation' (transit.py:17-18,176), and C4a shows a selective operation moves rho_B. Linearity (C4d), commuting local operations / tensor-product subsystems (C4b; 1607.01025 for gravity) and 'no closed causal loops' (Peres-Terno p.9) are never named. Meanwhile D13, D23, index3.py:1366 and axis.py:208-210 call the closure 'proved' on a board that also carries CTC (O3) and gravitational constructions. Recorded discrepancy, not an error: index3.py:1362 and paper/CLAIMS.md:4577 attribute 1.110e-16 to forty draws, but the forty give 2.220e-16.
audits.what_would_change_the_grade: To STANDS: the tree names H1-H4 at transit.py:17-18/176 and at D13/D23, and limits 'proved' to that class. To WRONG: a linear, completely positive, local, non-selective operation on A that changes rho_B. C1 rules this out as an algebraic identity, so only an error in C1's algebra could produce it. To DATA-DEPENDENT: a nonzero measured nonlinearity (currently |eps_gamma| < 4.7e-11, consistent with 0), or an established experimental failure of subsystem locality. To OPEN for the gravitational uses: D13's entangled limb being applied to a bulk or CTC carrier, where H3 and H4 are not established.

WHAT I CHECKED AT SOURCE (alphaXiv):
- Peres-Terno, quant-ph/0212023. Eq. (9), the commutator stated as a SUFFICIENT condition, is on p.8. Eqs. (10)->(11) are on pp.8-9: the sum over mu with sum E_mu = 1, then 'all expressions involving Alice's operators have totally disappeared'. 'we assume that there are no closed causal loops' is on p.9. Sec. III.D, p.13, says 'Replace superluminal by supersonic and the argument is exactly the same'. The eq. (16) incomplete Bell measurement and the 0.75 are on p.9.
- Ghirardi, 1305.2305. Eq. (12) and 'does not change in any way whatsoever' are on p.13. On p.14, under a selective measurement the distant physics 'is actually changed', the change depends on the outcome, and using it needs 'subluminal communication'. The paper cites GRW 1980 and Eberhard 1978, so marking both NAMED-NOT-READ is correct.
- Sorkin, gr-qc/9302018, p.6. Kick gives |d><d|, no kick gives I/2, measuring sigma_1 gives (1/4)|u><u| + (3/4)|d><d|. Sorkin also states that a measurement equals a random unitary intervention.
Every quotation the audit uses matches the source.

COMPUTATIONS:
- The rederive script runs 14/14 PASS, exit 0. I read the code. C1 is a genuine exact sympy identity over generic Kraus sets and a generic rho. C3 uses real Stinespring isometries. C4b matches Sorkin's numbers.
- My own read-only re-run of transit.py, using its own functions, gives 1.110e-16 for the 6 draws (seed 7) and 2.220e-16 for the 40 draws (seed 101). The discrepancy the audit records at index3.py:1362 and paper/CLAIMS.md:4577 is confirmed. It is a misattribution at machine epsilon, correctly logged as a discrepancy and not as an error.

WHY THE GRADE HOLDS:
- The grade rule (d67_audit.js:173) defines NARROWED as 'a hypothesis the tree drops'.
- transit.py names no hypothesis. A grep for linear, tensor, Kraus, CPTP, selective, CTC and hypothes finds only a code-section comment.
- The tree still writes 'IDENTICAL, AND PROVABLY SO' (transit.py docstring), 'provably ... because the no-communication theorem is a theorem' (index3.py:1366, axis.py:208-210) and 'the only route ... whose failure is proved' (index3.py:1366). It does this on a board that also carries gravitational and CTC rows; specthm R11 lists O3 beside D13 and D23.
- Linearity and complete positivity are load-bearing. 2412.20854, as restated, and C4d both show this. Tensor-product locality cannot be assumed once gravity enters (1607.01025, read by the audit).
- So the tree drops H1 and H3, and the definition gives NARROWED.
- The audit keeps the grade from implying WRONG and does not count it against the transit conclusion. That is right: every use the tree actually makes sits inside linear QM with local operations.

OVERSTATED, BUT THE GRADE DOES NOT DEPEND ON THEM:
(a) The H2 'weakened wording' item. B's UNCONDITIONAL reduced state does not change even when A makes a selective measurement, because B does not have A's outcome. Only the post-selected conditional state moves, which is what C4a computes and what Ghirardi p.14 describes. Read as B's own state, 'invariant under EVERY operation A can perform' is defensible. The audit itself concedes that the omission is 'in the wording, not in the physics'.
(b) The H4 attribution. Peres-Terno state 'no closed causal loops' in the paragraph AFTER the proof, about how classical signals order the interventions in time. The eq. (10)->(11) algebra does not use it, and C1 shows the identity needs no H4. In a CTC setting the theorem would break through nonlinear dynamics, which is H1, so H4 is a framework assumption and not a separate hypothesis of the identity.

ONE OMISSION, WHICH SUPPORTS THE GRADE: entangle.py:146 ('no-signalling is a theorem') is another use with no hypothesis named, and the audit does not list it.

Nothing I read or computed supports STANDS, WRONG, DATA-DEPENDENT or OPEN. The one datum that bears on the theorem is the measured bound |eps_gamma| < 4.7e-11 (2204.11875). It is consistent with zero and moves nothing.

I checked all four data rows and could not refute any of them.

Row 1 (no numerical inputs). This holds. Peres-Terno eqs. (9)-(11), which I read at quant-ph/0212023 pp.8-9, is a pure operator identity: it uses sum E_mu = 1 and no measured quantity. I re-ran the rederivation script and C1 confirms the identity exactly; the script passes 14/14 with exit 0.

Row 2 (transit.py instance). The figures are right. My own re-run, done independently of the audit's script, gives 1.1102e-16 for seed 7 over 6 draws and 2.2204e-16 for seed 101 over 40 draws. The selftest's '< 1e-14' is the real tolerance (transit.py:316-317), and it prints only the boolean. So the recorded discrepancy is real: index3.py:1362 and paper/CLAIMS.md:4577 attach 1.110e-16 to the forty draws, but 1.110e-16 is the worst of the six report draws. The audit records this as a misattribution at machine epsilon, not as an error, which is correct.

Row 3 (Proxima distance). foliation.py:583 sets PROXIMA_LY = 4.2465. PROXIMA_LY*LY = 4.0175e16 m. Because the tree's LY is c times the Julian year, '4.24650 Julian yr' is an identity, not a measurement; it is true but circular. Inverting the Gaia parallax 768.066539187357 mas gives 4.246460 +- 0.000276 ly, which matches the audit's 4.24646. moves_conclusion = 'no' follows: advantage_over_light(D) = D/c - D/c is identically zero, and D23 itself says 'ZERO BY CONSTRUCTION'.

Row 4 (experimental bound on nonlinearity). I read arXiv:2204.11875 at source. Page 3 gives eps_gamma = (0.7 +- 2.3)e-11 and |eps_gamma| < 4.7e-11 at 90% CL. Page 2 says the run took place in November 2021. All three match the audit's values.

One small over-statement, against the audit's own framing and not against the grade. The Kaplan-Rajendran modification is built to 'preserve causality' (p.1). Its observable effect appears only under the Everett reading and 'vanishes' under Copenhagen (p.2). The bound also assumes the universe 'dominantly evolved classically' (p.3). So this bound does not directly test the Gisin-type nonlinear dynamics that signal. The row's 'bounds one model class only' is accurate. But the what_would_change clause, 'To DATA-DEPENDENT: a nonzero measured nonlinearity', should be narrowed: a nonzero eps_gamma in this causal class would not by itself make the theorem data-dependent. This narrows the audit's reasoning; it is not a refutation.

lacked_data answers M's hypothesis with evidence in both directions; nothing in it is presumed. Inside its hypotheses the theorem is an algebraic identity, so no later datum can move it (C1). The later results that matter are about hypotheses, not data, and each was read at source: Sorkin on the measurement model, Gisin on linearity, Donnelly-Giddings on subsystem factorisation in gravity. None of them is a datum the 1978/1980 authors lacked that overturns the identity. The class-boundary limits are named as hypotheses (H1, H3, H4), not counted as refutations.

The data therefore supports NARROWED. The narrowing rests on the tree's dropped hypotheses, not on any data change.

audits.published_statement: Abstract (p.1): 'Since the ACA observations do not show any quiescent excess emission, we conclude that there is no need to invoke the presence of a dust belt at 1-4 AU. We also posit that the slight excess flux density of 101+-9 uJy observed in the 12-m observations compared to the photospheric flux density of 74+-4 uJy extrapolated from infrared wavelengths may be due to coronal heating from continual smaller flares ... If this is true, then the need for warm dust at ~0.4 AU is also removed.' Sec 4.2 (p.6): 'It is clear from our analysis that the entirety of the 1.3 mm emission detected by the ACA results from the short duration stellar flare. No emission is detected above a 3 sigma level during quiescence ... When averaged together with the remaining ~19 hours of non-detections, this transient event appeared as the ~340 uJy source detected by Anglada et al. (2017). Without the detection of a quiescent excess, there is no need to posit the cold belt at 1-4 AU.' ... 'the number of sources with flux density > 150 uJy that are expected within the ACA primary beam (FWHM ~39") is 13+10-8, a not insignificant number. In addition, Proxima Centauri sits close to the Galactic plane (latitude -2 deg) in a region of high background cirrus.' Sec 5 (p.7): the flare 'does not immediately impact the claim of an outer belt at ~30 AU', but background sources and cirrus 'suggest that caution should be used in over-interpreting this marginal result.' Sec 1 (p.1): 'Late M-type stars ... have long pre-main sequence phases during which the stellar luminosity can change significantly'.
published_hypotheses: H1 (data): the 2017 Jan 21 - Apr 25 ALMA 12-m (2 SBs, 41 antennas) and ACA (13 SBs, 8-11 7-m antennas) Band 6 data of programme 2016.A.00013.S. These are the same data Anglada et al. 2017 used; nothing new was observed.

H2 (sensitivity): 'no quiescent excess' holds at the ACA sensitivity: first-12 image rms 68 uJy/beam, no source above 3 sigma, a ~2 sigma central peak, and 30-s binning for short flares (p.3). A quiescent point source of ~100 uJy 'would not have been detected' (p.3).
H3 (parsimony, not exclusion): the belt conclusion is 'no need to posit/invoke'. The evidence for the belt is removed; the paper does not claim to exclude a belt below its sensitivity.
H4 (photosphere): the 74+-4 uJy at 1.3 mm is an extrapolation of the Ribas et al. 2017 SED model, not a measurement.

H5 (conditional, coronal): the 12-m ~30 uJy excess 'may be' / 'could also be plausibly explained by' / is 'likely' due to continual small flares (by analogy with AU Mic). The 0.4 au warm dust is removed only 'if this is true'.

H6 (background): the 13+10-8 figure uses 1.3 mm differential counts (Carniani et al. 2015) over 'the ACA primary beam (FWHM ~39")'; neither the integration area nor the formula is stated. A second contamination source is Galactic (latitude -2 deg, high cirrus) and is not quantified.
H7 (outer belt): the ACA visibilities 'do not adequately cover the short spatial frequencies' needed to measure the total disk flux, and the flare 'does not immediately impact' the 30 au claim.
hypothesis_drift: STRENGTHENED (the load-bearing drift): formation.py:288-289 says 'THE 1-4 au BELT, which would have held small primitive bodies, IS WITHDRAWN'; formation.py:43-44 and :410 say 'MacGregor 2018 withdraws Anglada 2017's 1-4 au belt'; formation.py:458 sets SURVEY_BELT_1_4AU_WITHDRAWN_BY_SOURCE = True. The source says 'no need to posit' (p.6) and 'no need to invoke' (p.1, p.7): the evidence is removed (H3). Computed here, the first-12 ACA image disfavours star + Anglada's ~200 uJy belt at ~2.0 sigma, and Anglada's full 340 uJy at ~3.0 sigma. A belt fainter than ~130 uJy is not excluded, and such a belt could still hold small bodies. 'Withdraws' also names an author act, and MacGregor et al. are not the Anglada authors. The one discover_papers call found no response from Anglada et al.; that is a failure to find one, not a finding that none exists. The tree's quote at :286-287 is verbatim-correct; the drift is in the gloss.
DROPPED (sensitivity scope): formation.py:286-289 drops H2. The 'no quiescent excess' holds at first-12 rms 68 uJy/beam, and a ~2 sigma central peak is present (p.3).

DROPPED (second contamination source): formation.py:290-291 and :448-449 carry the 13+10-8 background count but drop the Galactic-plane / cirrus caveat (p.6, p.7). This weakens no conclusion the tree draws.

UNSTATED INPUT CARRIED AS READ: formation.py:290-291 quotes '13+10-8 background sources > 150 uJy expected in the primary beam' exactly, but the paper states neither area nor formula. Recomputed from the counts it cites, the figure is ~1.6 in the FWHM disk.

NO DRIFT: formation.py:289-290 (0.4 au warm dust unnecessary 'if' the excess is coronal) keeps the conditional. formation.py:447 ('~1 min flare') matches p.3. formation.py:275-277 (PMS luminosity) is verbatim from Sec 1. formation.py:293-294 (Proxima b m_p sin i = 1.3 M_earth, a = 0.05 AU) matches Sec 1.
