verifiers.reason:
Not refuted. The grade NARROWED holds and the data rows are substantially right. Reading at source turns most of the audit's snippet-only figures into READ figures. It also finds three discrepancies and one omission. Each is recorded as found, not repaired. None of them moves 'no confirmed identification'.

CONFIRMED AT SOURCE
(1) SQLS row, 1303.1301. Abstract on p.1 and the Fig.3 text on p.4: 'There are no multiple images ... for ~50000 distant quasars' (N_Q = 50,836), and 'n < 10^-4 h^3 Mpc^-3 for a range of the throat radius a = 10 - 10^4 pc'. H-STAT is now READ: p.3 says 'We assume that the number density of the lens is constant in comoving scale'. p.1 confirms the galactic microlensing sensitivity of 100-1e7 km (Abe 2010) as a sensitivity only, with no bound. Recomputed: Wigner-Seitz radius 13.37 Mpc/h; 419 objects within 100 Mpc/h; 1193 km lies 11.41 orders below 10 pc. Two refinements: the axis is in h^-1 pc, which gives 11.57 orders; and p.4 extends the bound qualitatively to a = 0.1-1e5 pc, which gives 9.41 orders. The 'no window reaches 1193 km' conclusion survives both.
(2) GWTC-3 TGR, 2112.06861. Abstract: 'no evidence for ... post-merger echoes'. Table XIV gives p-values from 0.18 to 0.89 over 15 O3b events, from a morphology-independent search. Confirmed. The row's moves_conclusion ('No, toward null') follows.
(3) Shadow row, 2509.13715. p.11 reads verbatim 'Wormholes can mimic black hole shadows but have different quasinormal mode (QNM) spectra due to the absence of a true horizon', and detection is framed throughout as a prospect. This confirms detect.py:29-31 and the H-ID reading, which is now READ rather than READ-VIA-RESTATEMENT.
(4) Abedi 1612.00266 makes no wormhole claim. Its abstract claims 'Planck-scale structure near black hole horizons' (firewall/fuzzball). The audit is right on this.

DISCREPANCIES (recorded as discrepancies, not refutations)
(a) Echo row value_then '~2.9 sigma'. This quotes negmass.py:16 faithfully, but at source it is the superseded v1 figure. 1712.09966 p.1: 'claimed in [20] ... p-value 3.7e-3 ... 2.9 sigma (... one-sided ... 2.7 sigma). This was subsequently updated to a p-value of ~1% and interpreted as 2.5 sigma'. The published v2 headline (1612.00266 abstract) is p = 0.011, 2.5 sigma. 2.9 sigma survives in v2 only as an appendix maximum at gamma = 0.93, which the authors caution is 'less reliable'. Westerweck's reanalysis gives p = 0.02-0.032 (about 2.1-2.3 sigma), and 0.199 without LVT151012. This strengthens the move toward null.
(b) Femtolensing row 'n < 2e-9 AU^-3 for a ~ 1 cm'. At source (1302.7170, pp.11-12), 2e-9 is the bound on compact objects of M ~ 3e18 g, from Barnacka et al. For Ellis wormholes the paper states only a rough 'n <~ 10^-9 AU^-3' at a ~ 0.7 cm, and says 'we do not distinguish between the point mass lenses and Ellis wormholes'. It is a translation of a compact-object null, not a wormhole search. The Wigner-Seitz radius becomes 620 AU rather than 492. Conclusion unaffected.
(c) The audit's H-MODEL and window comparison sets the tree's target against Ellis windows. But the target in detect.py is a Morris-Thorne throat r0 = 1193 km carrying 32.13 Msun (recomputed from exotic_mass_solar), and negmass.py:393-400 says 'the thing to look for has a mass'. Ellis is massless (1303.1301 p.1). Throat-radius windows are therefore not the governing comparison.

OMISSION, which bears on 'premise unpriced is accurate at the target'
If the target lenses as a ~32 Msun point mass, and 1302.7170 shows geometric-optics lensing cannot tell such a lens from a wormhole, then compact-object microlensing does price its abundance. OGLE, 2403.02386 p.3, READ: 'M = 10 Msun f = 1.2%; M = 100 Msun f = 3.0%' at 95%, for 'any compact objects'. Log-interpolated, this gives f < ~1.9% of halo dark matter at 32 Msun. The audit's claim that the premise stays unpriced at 1193 km therefore holds only for a massless (Ellis or M_ADM = 0) object. For the massive target that detect.py actually names, an upper bound exists, conditional on the hypothesis that the ADM mass is ~32 Msun, which is not established in the tree. This narrows the 'unpriced' half further; it does not favour M.

M's HYPOTHESIS
It is answered with evidence both ways, not presumed. Every channel read at source is null or a superseded or contested tentative claim, so no datum moves the conclusion. The deciding data, a discriminating channel at the right size and model, do not exist. audits.published_statement:
Not re-read in this stage. The tree quotes it at qeihps.py:319-322 (KONTOU_ON_ABSOLUTE_FOR_NMC): 'This is not true, for example, for the T_split operator of nonminimally coupled fields, so these inequalities cannot be used in this case. State-dependent bounds have been derived for the nonminimally coupled field [17,29,30].' The tree does not quote what 'This' refers to.

The primary sources READ identify the property that fails as the one the Fewster-Smith absolute QEI depends on:
- FS eq. (80) writes the minimally coupled T_split as the symmetric sum of squares 1/2 sum_alpha e_alpha^a nabla_a (x) e_alpha^b nabla_b.
- FS Sec. 2.2: 'our argument relies crucially on being able to write T_split in a symmetric form ... A similar problem arises for the non-minimally coupled scalar field. In this case one must smear the stress-energy tensor even to obtain an inequality on the classical field'.
- FO abstract: averages are 'unbounded from below on the class of Hadamard states'; there is a state-dependent generalised QEI 'for coupling constants in the range 0 < xi <= 1/4' on globally hyperbolic curved spacetimes.
- FO Sec. 6: '(at least for massless fields in four-dimensional Minkowski space) ... cannot obey QEIs ... in which there is a state-independent lower bound'. Also from Sec. 6: an absolute version 'can also be adapted to the non-minimally coupled field'.
- FFKP Sec. IV: 'a difference QEIs unlike the absolute one that was possible for the minimally coupled field ... the strongest bound we will be able to derive is state-dependent'.
published_hypotheses: Kontou, as quoted: the operator is T_split of a non-minimally coupled scalar (xi != 0). The failing property is whatever 'these inequalities' (the earlier QEI derivations in Sec. 3.2) require. The tree does not quote the antecedent, and it was not re-read here.

FS gr-qc/0702056 (READ): the absolute QEI needs T_split written in a symmetric sum-of-squares (positive-type) form. It also assumes minimal coupling, a 4D globally hyperbolic spacetime and Hadamard states.
FO 0708.2450, Secs. 3 and 6 (READ): the no-go against any state-independent bound is proved for xi > 0, massless, 4D Minkowski only. It is not proved for xi < 0, for m > 0, or on curved backgrounds.

FO Thm 4.2 (READ): a state-dependent DIFFERENCE QEI. Hypotheses: 0 < xi <= 1/4, a timelike geodesic, a globally hyperbolic curved spacetime, Hadamard states, and normal ordering against a reference Hadamard state.
FFKP Thm IV.1 (READ): a state-dependent DIFFERENCE null QEI. Hypotheses: any xi, a curved globally hyperbolic spacetime, a small sampling domain, Hadamard states.
FO Sec. 6 (READ): an ABSOLUTE version for NMC is expected ('can also be adapted'). Absolute and state-independent are different properties, so absoluteness is not excluded; it just has not been done.
hypothesis_drift: qeihps.py:46-47 paraphrases Kontou as saying 'no absolute or state-independent inequality reaches this field'. The quoted sentence only says 'these inequalities cannot be used', meaning the positive-type (Fewster-Smith-class) derivations. FO Sec. 6 (READ) expects an absolute, state-dependent NMC QEI to be adaptable. The paraphrase therefore DROPS the qualifier 'of the FS sum-of-squares class'. The tree's own records at qeihps.py:90 and :511 (ABSOLUTE_QEI_FOR_NMC = NOT-FOUND, 'can also be adapted (expected, not done)') have the correct scope. The drift is confined to one prose line and reaches no value.

The canonical.json name for this key says 'only state-dependent bounds exist', with hypotheses 'xi != 0, T_split'. Kontou, as quoted, says state-dependent bounds 'have been derived', not that no other kind can exist. That no state-independent bound exists is FO's theorem, which assumes xi > 0, massless, 4D Minkowski, so the canonical summary DROPS 'xi > 0', 'm = 0' and 'Minkowski'. The owner file keeps them (qeihps.py:86-90: 'FOR THE MASSLESS FIELD IN 4D MINKOWSKI SPACE ... NOT proved on HPS's curved background').
The status word 'READ' at qeihps.py:318-322 matches DOCKET 64's record, but this stage could not re-verify it. This is an unverified attribution, not a drift.

No drift was found in the values that rest on this result. FEWSTER_SMITH_ON_HPS (qeihps.py:500) refuses FS because FS require minimal coupling, a hypothesis FS state themselves. ABSOLUTE_QEI_FOR_NMC (qeihps.py:511), quoted at specthm.py:1043-1044 (R6), says NOT-FOUND/expected, which agrees with FO Sec. 6.

data_at_publication.quantity: None. The result is a structural statement about the form of the point-split stress operator and which QEI derivations apply to it. No measured or fitted number enters the conclusion.
data_at_publication.value_now: n/a
data_at_publication.moves_conclusion: No. The coupling xi enters only through its sign and whether it is zero (re-derivation checks C1 and D'). HPS's xi = 1/6 is a model choice (conformal coupling, gr-qc/9701064), not a measurement.

rederivation.outcome:
All 9 checks pass (sympy 1.14.0, z3 5.1.0).
- A: at xi = 0 the classical T_00 equals FS eq. (80)'s sum of squares exactly (sympy).
- B: from FO eq. (7), T_00 = 1/2 phidot^2 + (1/2 - 2xi)|grad phi|^2 - 2xi phi Lap(phi) + K phi^2 (sympy). At a point in normal coordinates every curvature and mass term multiplies phi^2 and is carried as a free coefficient K.
- C1: z3 returns UNSAT for 'some xi != 0 and K give rho >= 0 for every jet'. So for every xi != 0 and every K there is Cauchy data with classical rho < 0 at the point.
- C1': the explicit witness L = (K+1)/(2xi) gives rho = -1 exactly, so the UNSAT is not vacuous.
- C2: z3 confirms that xi = 0 with K >= 0 forces rho >= 0.
- C3: the (phi, Lap phi) block has eigenvalues +-xi, so it is indefinite whenever xi != 0.
- D: at HPS's xi = 1/6, the datum phi = A(1 + c r^2) (times a bump) gives rho(0) = -2cA^2 < 0.
- D': for general xi, rho(0) = -12 xi c A^2.
A sum-of-squares T_split forces classical rho >= 0 (by hand: rho = sum_i (P_i phi)^2). C1 is the contrapositive: for every xi != 0, of either sign and in any spacetime, the NMC T_split is not of the positive-type form the FS / Fewster derivations use. That is what the quoted sentence asserts.
Not re-run here: FO's quantum no-go, which is a construction of Hadamard states (READ at source, not re-derived), and the exact wording of Kontou Sec. 3.2.

later_literature.ref: C. J. Fewster & L. W. Osterbrink, arXiv:0708.2450 (J. Phys. A 41 (2008) 025402), Kontou's [30]

It derives a state-dependent difference QEI for 0 < xi <= 1/4 on globally hyperbolic curved spacetimes. It expects an absolute version to be adaptable but does not derive one. This paper is earlier than Kontou and was read as a primary source, not as later literature.

audits.lacked_data:
This tests M's hypothesis for this result.

The result contains no measured datum. It is a statement about the algebraic form of the point-split stress operator (whether it is a sum of squares) and about which proof techniques apply to it.

Evidence against a missing-data defect: the failure of positivity is re-derived here from the classical stress tensor alone. z3 shows it for every xi != 0 and every value of the curvature/mass coefficient. No future measurement of xi, m or the background could restore the sum-of-squares form; only xi = 0 exactly does.

Evidence for M's direction (incompleteness, not error): what is missing is a theorem, not data.
- FO say an absolute NMC QEI 'can also be adapted' but do not derive one.
- FO's no-go against state-independent bounds is proved only for xi > 0, massless, 4D Minkowski. For xi < 0, for massive fields and on curved backgrounds such as HPS, what is established is only that the positive-type method does not apply, not that no state-independent bound exists.

The tree already carries this incompleteness at qeihps.py:86-90 and :511, and in specthm R6.

Effect on the tree's conclusions: none in either direction. FEWSTER_SMITH_ON_HPS is refused because FS require minimal coupling, independently of this sentence. ABSOLUTE_QEI_FOR_NMC stays NOT-FOUND.
audits.grade_evidence:
The mathematical content of the quoted sentence holds and is machine-checked:
- The NMC point-split energy density is not of sum-of-squares form, for every xi != 0 and any curvature or mass coefficient (z3 checks C1 and C1').
- At HPS's xi = 1/6, rho(0) = -2cA^2 < 0 (sympy check D).
- At xi = 0 it is exactly FS eq. (80) (sympy check A, z3 check C2).
- FO and FFKP, both READ, do derive state-dependent bounds.

It is NARROWED as the tree phrases it, in two places:
1. qeihps.py:46-47 says 'no absolute or state-independent inequality reaches this field'. This drops the qualifier that it is the FS positive-type class that fails. FO Sec. 6 (READ) expects an absolute, state-dependent NMC QEI to be adaptable.
2. The canonical summary says 'only state-dependent bounds exist' for xi != 0. The non-existence of any state-independent bound is FO's theorem for xi > 0, massless, 4D Minkowski only.

Neither narrowing reaches a value the tree uses. qeihps.py:86-90 and :511 carry FO's scope, FEWSTER_SMITH_ON_HPS rests on FS's own minimal-coupling hypothesis, and specthm R6 quotes ABSOLUTE_QEI_FOR_NMC = NOT-FOUND.

It is not WRONG: nothing is contradicted.

Caveat on attribution: the verbatim Kontou wording and the antecedent of 'This' were not re-read in this stage (alphaXiv quota used up, arXiv hosts refused by egress policy). The attribution rests on DOCKET 64's recorded reading. Any wording difference found on a re-read is a discrepancy to record, not a refutation.
audits.what_would_change_the_grade:
To STANDS, three things are needed:
- qeihps.py:46-47 reads 'no absolute QEI of the Fewster-Smith sum-of-squares type, and no state-independent QEI, is known to reach this field'.
- The canonical summary carries FO's 'xi > 0, massless, 4D Minkowski' for the non-existence reading.
- A re-read of Kontou Sec. 3.2 confirms the quotation and what 'This' refers to.

To OPEN: a re-read shows that Kontou's 'This' refers to something other than the symmetric (positive-type) form of T_split. The attribution would then be unsupported, although the physics checked here still holds.

Further NARROWED, but still not WRONG: a post-2024 paper derives an absolute or state-independent QEI for NMC fields on a class that contains HPS. That would also flip ABSOLUTE_QEI_FOR_NMC from NOT-FOUND and would need its own audit.

To WRONG: a sum-of-squares decomposition of T_split at xi != 0. Re-derivation check C1 shows none can exist.

verifiers.reason:
The NARROWED grade survives. I read Kontou at source, which the auditor could not do (alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries on 2405.05963v2, p.9 of 28). The tree's quotation at qeihps.py:318-322 is verbatim. The antecedent of 'This' is the sentence before it: 'This is done by utilizing the fact that, for free fields, the operator T_split is of the positive type and symmetric.' 'These inequalities' are Fewster's general difference QEI [27] and the Fewster-Smith absolute QEI [28] (eq. 40). So the audit's route to OPEN is closed: Kontou means exactly the property the audit inferred. The read status of the Kontou passage should move from NAMED-NOT-READ to READ.

**Narrowing 1 holds.** Kontou says only that these two positive-type derivations cannot be used. qeihps.py:46-47 has her saying why NO absolute or state-independent inequality reaches the field. Her text does not rule out an absolute one, and FO's conclusion (src/0708.2450.txt:3846-3847) expects one can be adapted.

**Narrowing 2 holds but is weaker than the audit puts it.**
- What was proved: FO's construction, for xi > 0, massless, 4D Minkowski. That is still the only proof read.
- What is asserted without FO's qualifiers:
  - Fewster, math-ph/0611058 (GRG 39, 1855), READ: NMC fields 'do not obey state-independent QEIs'.
  - Fewster-Kontou 1809.05047, READ: an N-copy argument from classical violation, 'even in Minkowski space'.
- Both cite FO for the detailed argument. So the canonical summary dropping 'xi > 0, m = 0, Minkowski' is a drift in what is PROVED, not in what the field's authors assert.

**Re-derivation re-run.** The auditor's script passes all checks: A, B, C1, C1', C2, C3, D, D'.

**Missed by the audit, and it does not move the grade.**
- Kontou's [29] is Fewster & Kontou, PRD 99 (2019) 045001, arXiv:1809.05047. Its intro states: 'as shown in Ref. [28], nonminimally coupled fields obey state dependent QWEIs of both absolute and difference types'.
- I read that [28] (math-ph/0611058). It only redefines 'absolute QI' so that state-dependent bounds count (Def. 3.1). Its App. B presents FO's DIFFERENCE QEI for 0 <= xi <= 1/4. No absolute NMC QEI is derived.
- This is a published attribution discrepancy that should be recorded beside ABSOLUTE_QEI_FOR_NMC (qeihps.py:511). It is not a refutation: NOT-FOUND stands on the sources read.

**Nothing moves the grade.**
- Nothing supports STANDS. The paraphrase at qeihps.py:46-47 still over-reads 'these' as 'any absolute'.
- Nothing supports WRONG. No source contradicts the sentence, and z3 C1 excludes a sum-of-squares T_split at xi != 0.

The re-run reproduces the audit. I ran the copy at scratchpad/d67/verify/rederive/2405.05963-sec3.2.py and all 9 checks pass (A, B, C1, C1', C2, C3, D, D'), exit code 0.

ENCODING. Check B is the standard non-minimally coupled T_00 in signature (+,-,-,-): rho = 1/2 phidot^2 + (1/2-2xi)|grad phi|^2 - 2xi phi Lap phi + m^2 phi^2/2. Check A matches Fewster-Smith eq. (80) at xi = 0.

The z3 jet encoding is faithful. (phi, phidot, grad phi, Lap phi) at a point are free Cauchy data. T_00 contains no phi-double-dot, because the Box term minus the second time derivative cancels it. So rho is evaluated on real solutions, and rewriting the operator with the field equation cannot rescue a sum-of-squares form. Two parts of this rest on prose argument rather than machine checks:
- the claim that every curvature term enters only as K phi^2 (the Christoffel symbols vanish at the origin of Riemann normal coordinates);
- the contrapositive 'a sum of squares implies rho >= 0'.
Both are elementary and correct.

What the script checks is a LEMMA. The NMC point-split operator is not of pointwise sum-of-squares (positive-type) form for any xi != 0, of either sign. It does not check the quantum theorem: Fewster-Osterbrink's no-go against a state-independent bound is not re-run. The audit says this itself (agrees_with_source 'partly'), so it is not passing off a toy as the theorem. One gap remains: the check does not consider positive-type forms that only appear after integrating by parts along the worldline. That is minor and does not change the grade.

VACUITY GUARDS (script vacuity_2405.05963-sec3.2.py), all as expected:
- V1: C1 with the hypothesis negated (xi = 0) is SAT, with K = 0.
- V2: dropping the phi*Lap(phi) term at xi = 1/6 gives SAT. That term is what makes rho negative.
- V3: C2 with K < 0 is SAT, so the K >= 0 condition matters.
- V4: the same quantified query with a manifestly positive rho is SAT, so the ForAll encoding is not trivially UNSAT.
- V5: C1 is UNSAT separately for xi > 0 and for xi < 0.
- V6: flipping the sign of the xi term makes identity B fail.
- V7: the witness jet is realised by phi = 1 + L r^2/6.
The UNSAT results are therefore not vacuous.

SOURCES. The grep cross-checks the audit cites are present in the cached extractions:
- 0708.2450 lines 19, 3810 ('at least for massless') and 3846-3847 ('can also be adapted to the non-minimally coupled field');
- 2309.10848 lines 2328-2330 ('difference QEIs unlike the absolute ... state-dependent');
- 0702056 lines 1018-1024 ('symmetric form', 'similar problem arises for the non-minimally coupled scalar field').

The owner lines match the audit's account:
- qeihps.py:46-47 says 'no absolute or state-independent inequality reaches this field';
- qeihps.py:86-90 keeps FO's scope (xi > 0, massless, 4D Minkowski, not proved on HPS);
- qeihps.py:511 has ABSOLUTE_QEI_FOR_NMC = NOT-FOUND, 'expected, not done'.

GRADE. NARROWED is supported. The mathematics holds and is machine-checked. The paraphrase at line 46 and the canonical name ('only state-dependent bounds exist') are both narrowed:
- they drop the qualifier 'Fewster-Smith positive-type class';
- they drop FO's hypotheses xi > 0, m = 0 and Minkowski for the non-existence reading.
No value the tree uses is affected.

One softness on the first narrowing. If 'reaches' is read as 'is known to reach', line 46 is true as of NOT-FOUND, so that narrowing is borderline. The canonical summary's narrowing stands regardless.

Kontou's wording was not re-read here either; the alphaXiv quota and egress are unchanged. The attribution therefore stays unverified and is not upgraded.

audits.published_statement: Fewster-Olum-Pfenning gr-qc/0609007 p.10: '[the] spacetime obtained by periodically identifying Minkowski space along the z-direction. The ground state of the massless, minimally coupled scalar field on this (globally hyperbolic) spacetime has renormalized stress tensor <T_ab> = (pi^2/(90 L^4)) diag(-1, 1, 1, -3) (24) where L is the periodicity length. It is readily verified that the (A)NEC is violated along any null geodesic with a nonzero z-component of velocity, i.e., for those which wind around the compact direction. On the other hand, the (A)NEC is obeyed along complete null geodesics with zero velocity in the z-direction ... null geodesics which wind round the cylinder are not achronal.' p.11: 'distant interactions or boundary conditions apparently do not help to produce ANEC violations. For example, Casimir plates would not seem to be useful to support a wormhole ... because of the need to get through the plate.' Kuo-Ford gr-qc/9304008 eqs.(3.32)-(3.33): '... = -(zeta(4)/(pi^2 L^4)) diag[1,-1,-1,3] ... we have excluded the n = 0 term, since it is just the contribution from the Minkowski vacuum. Since zeta(4) = pi^4/90, <:T_00(x):> = -pi^2/(90 L^4).' GJW 1608.05687 sec. 5 (the tree's context, prose only): 'the negative ANE could be understood as coming from the Casimir effect associated to the cycle in space ... Of course, the effect would be enhanced if the signals sent between the black holes were directed and amplified (otherwise the Casimir energy would be extremely tiny if the black holes were far apart).'
published_hypotheses: H1 field content: ONE free, massless, real scalar (minimally coupled; in flat space without boundaries the conformal improvement adds nothing since <phi^2> is constant). Other fields change the coefficient (EM: 2 dof).

H2 geometry: flat Minkowski space with ONE periodic spatial identification of length L, infinite and homogeneous in the transverse directions; the density is UNIFORM. No wormhole, no curvature, no throat.
H3 state: the ground (vacuum) state of the identified spacetime, zero temperature; renormalised by subtracting the Minkowski (n = 0) term.

H4 the negative quantity is the energy density T_00 = -pi^2/(90 L^4); the null-null component is -4 pi^2/(90 L^4) along geodesics that wind the compact direction and ZERO along null geodesics transverse to it (FOP p.10); ANEC is violated only on non-achronal (winding) geodesics.

H5 semiclassical: <T_ab> is an expectation value; Kuo-Ford's paper is precisely about the fluctuations around it, which are not small in general (their abstract: semiclassical theory 'a good approximation only when the fluctuations in the stress tensor are small').

H6 (GJW context) the flat-space Casimir reading of the cycle is a discussion-section remark with no computation; GJW state the undirected effect is 'extremely tiny' at large separation and that directing/amplifying the signals would enhance it.

audits.lacked_data: M's hypothesis tested for this result. The formula is a theorem of free QFT on a flat identified spacetime, and the only numerical inputs are hbar, c (exact since 2019) and G (22 ppm); the tree's constants are current and CODATA 2022 moves the gain by 6e-10 relative. No experiment measures a periodic-identification Casimir density, and the plate-force measurements (sibling audit) confirm the Lifshitz/ideal framework, with every real-material correction REDUCING |rho|. So for this result the authors lacked no DATUM that changes the conclusion: evidence AGAINST M's hypothesis on the data side. What was missing in 2016 (GJW remark) was a CONSTRUCTION, not data: GJW named 'directed and amplified' signals without quantifying them, and the tree quantified only the undirected single-scalar version. MMP (2018) and Butcher (2014) supply constructions whose negative energy does not follow the single-length pi^2/(90 L^4) law; that is a hypothesis the tree's model drops (H2), not an inaccuracy in the older mathematics. Neither construction reaches metre-scale separation with Standard Model content (MMP: d below the electroweak length; Butcher: static wormhole not stabilised, metre-long throat has radius ~6e-25 m), so having the later results narrows the class the tree's number describes without overturning the tree's metre-scale refusal.
audits.grade_evidence: The external result STANDS on its hypotheses: rho = -pi^2 hbar c/(90 L^4), <T_ab> = (pi^2/(90 L^4)) diag(-1,1,1,-3), re-derived two independent ways (sympy, exact) and matching FOP eq.(24) and Kuo-Ford eq.(3.33) as read; the tree's numbers (2.167e-28 Pa, 9.505e43 Pa, 4.3866e71 D^2, 0.0934 l_P) reproduce exactly and equal the closed form 360 D^2/(pi l_P^2); no datum has moved (CODATA 2022: 6e-10). The TREE'S USE is broader than the result: (1) phase1.py:403-404 quotes the figure without its model hypotheses -- one free scalar, flat transversely infinite uniform density, a single length D, cycle 2D -- and gjw.py:94-100 reads the resulting Planck landing as independent evidence when it is forced by the single-length model (D4); later literature (Butcher 2014, MMP 2018, read) shows Casimir-type sources with two lengths or 2D-reduced modes that escape that law, so '4.39e71 short' holds for the undirected flat-cycle scalar model, not for Casimir support as a class. (2) DISCREPANCY: energy density divided into a T_kk threshold; the winding-direction T_kk is 4|rho| (gain 1.097e71 D^2). ADM's shell self-energy result was read as restated by G. Dillon, arXiv:1303.2706v3 eqs (2),(6),(7). Bartnik 1986 and Chrusciel 1986 are NAMED-NOT-READ (restated by McCormick).

audits.published_statement: EHLS 1110.2087v2 Def. 3: 'If (M, g, k) is asymptotically flat, one can define the ADM energy E and the ADM momentum P as E = 1/(2(n-1)omega_{n-1}) lim_{r->inf} int_{|x|=r} sum (g_ij,i - g_ii,j) nu^j dH^{n-1} ...'. McCormick 2401.05128v1 Def. 2.2: the same flux, and 'By the work of Bartnik [10] and Chrusciel [26] it is now well-known that the ADM mass is well-defined and independent of the diffeomorphism phi used to define it ... asymptotic flatness alone is not sufficient to ensure that the ADM mass is in fact finite, however with the additional assumption that scalar curvature is integrable it turns out to be the case.' For n = 3 the prefactor is 1/(16 pi). With g_ij = (1 - 2 Phi) delta_ij this gives E = lim r^2 Phi'(r) (derived here, C1). So E equals the coefficient of the 1/r tail of Phi exactly when the SPATIAL metric carries the same Phi as g_tt.
published_hypotheses: H1: an asymptotically flat end. There is a compact K and a chart M\K ~ R^3\B in which g - delta = O(r^-tau), dg = O(r^-tau-1), d^2g = O(r^-tau-2), with tau > 1/2 (McCormick Def. 2.1; EHLS Def. 3 has the weighted-Sobolev form).
H2: finiteness needs integrable scalar curvature on top of H1. Chart independence under H1+H2 is due to Bartnik 1986 and Chrusciel 1986 (NAMED-NOT-READ, restated by McCormick).
H3: E is a flux of the SPATIAL metric g_ij, not of g_tt. The identification 'E = coefficient of 1/r in Phi' holds when g_ij = (1 - 2 Phi) delta_ij + o(1/r).

H4: the definition is kinematic. No field equation or energy condition enters, and the mass it assigns includes gravitational binding energy (ADM shell result via Dillon eq (7); de Aguiar Alves-Costa 2503.18963: 'mass is more than the sum of its parts').
H5: only the end matters. Regularity inside K does not enter the definition.
hypothesis_drift: NONE on H1 or H3 for the metric as written. concentric.py:163-168 (the potential) together with composite.py:35 and :133-137 (ds^2 = -(1+2Phi)dt^2 + (1-2Phi)dx^2) put the same Phi into g_ij, so the monopole of Phi IS the ADM flux. g - delta = m a^2/r^3 + O(r^-5), so the decay tau = 3 is well above 1/2 (C3). This depends on composite.py's isotropic form (Psi = Phi), a condition concentric.py:178 does not name.

WEAKENED (linearisation scoped too narrowly). concentric.py:37-38 lists M_ADM = 0 among the things that are 'unaffected', and concentric.py:139-141 says linearisation moves only 'the window's edges'. For the prescribed metric E = 0 is exact (C3). But reading this as 'core of mass -m plus shell of mass +m, so the monopoles cancel' (concentric.py:42-50) identifies E with the sum of linear source monopoles, and that holds only to first order in m/a (H4). A Newtonian post-linear ESTIMATE of the binding term is -0.074 m at m = 5e-3 and -0.29 m at m = 2e-2 (C8). So 'M_ADM = 0 EXACTLY' (concentric.py:49, 77, 352) is exact at the metric level and only first-order at the matter level.

DROPPED (vacuum exterior / compact support). stability.py:16-19 takes 'concentric.py's device' to have 'INTERIOR Schwarzschild M_in = -m' and 'EXTERIOR M_out = 0, i.e. FLAT MINKOWSKI'. source.located: The explicit coefficient formula S(zeta)|0> = (cosh r)^{-1/2} sum_k (-e^{i delta} tanh r)^k sqrt((2k)!)/(2^k k!) |2k> is a textbook quantum-optics result. Its classic sources are D. Stoler, PRD 1, 3217 (1970); H.P. Yuen, PRA 13, 2226 (1976); C.M. Caves, PRD 23, 1693 (1981); R. Loudon & P.L. Knight, J. Mod. Opt. 34, 709 (1987); and Gerry & Knight (2005). None of them is on arXiv, and the owner cites no source. The paper the owner is auditing, Kuo & Ford arXiv:gr-qc/9304008 v1 (1993), supplies the convention the formula must match (eqs 3.9-3.17, citing Caves 1981 as its ref [8]) and the qualitative Fock statement.

audits.published_statement: This statement is not quoted from any page read in this stage. The standard statement, in Kuo-Ford's convention (KF 3.11 and 3.16, both READ): for S(zeta) = exp[(zeta* a^2 - zeta a+^2)/2] with zeta = r e^{i delta}, S(zeta)|0> = (cosh r)^{-1/2} SUM_k (-e^{i delta} tanh r)^k sqrt((2k)!)/(2^k k!) |2k>. KF print verbatim (p.8) that the squeezed vacuum is 'a superposition of states containing even numbers of particles', and that 'we may also take delta = 0, as this is simply a choice of phase'. The tree's form (fluctuation.py:427) is cs[2k] = (-t)^k sqrt((2k)!)/(2^k k!)/sqrt(cosh r) with t = tanh r, which is the delta = 0 instance.
published_hypotheses: H1 single bosonic mode, [a, a+] = 1, Fock vacuum a|0> = 0
H2 squeeze convention S(zeta) = exp[(zeta* a^2 - zeta a+^2)/2], i.e. S+ a S = a cosh r - a+ e^{i delta} sinh r (KF 3.11, 3.16 READ). The opposite convention flips the sign of (-e^{i delta} t)^k
H3 zeta = r e^{i delta} can be any complex number. The series converges for every finite r because tanh r < 1, using sum_k C(2k,k)(t^2/4)^k = (1-t^2)^{-1/2}

audits.name: Cauchy-Schwarz inequality SUM G_AB^2 >= (tr G)^2/4 on a 4x4 symmetric matrix

source.located: Classic sources: Cauchy, Cours d'analyse (1821), Note II (the discrete form); Bunyakovsky (1859, the integral form); Schwarz (1885). None of the originals has an arXiv copy.
source.via: I did not read the originals (NAMED-NOT-READ). I read two arXiv restatements from alphaXiv page text cached at scratchpad/d67/src/casmag/all/. (i) arXiv:2312.03478v2, Sec. 2.2, Theorem 1: 'Let x, y in R^n. Then |x . y| <= ||x|| . ||y||. The equality in CBS inequality holds if and only if the vectors x and y are collinear.' (lines 295-305, md5 dc2a9a33e63238cbff44859bdccb8a25). (ii) arXiv:2504.19543v1, p.2 eq.(1): Bunyakovsky's 'well-known inequality' (a1^2+...+an^2)(b1^2+...+bn^2) > (a1b1+...+anbn)^2, which refers to Note II of Cauchy's 1821 lectures (md5 6d3233c32b77bed54ca672061737dfc8). In this stage I tried answer_pdf_queries, get_paper_content and discover_papers, and all three returned 'alphaXiv assistant quota exceeded'. The Kuo & Ford paper the tree applies this to (gr-qc/9304008) was read earlier in DOCKET 67 (src/gr-qc_9304008.note). The result is pure finite real algebra, so a complete exact proof is given here and nothing depends on the unread originals.

audits.published_statement: For real a, b in R^n: (SUM a_i^2)(SUM b_i^2) >= (SUM a_i b_i)^2, i.e. |a.b| <= ||a|| ||b||, with equality iff a and b are collinear (2312.03478 Thm 1; Cauchy 1821 Note II as restated in 2504.19543 eq.(1), which prints the strict form). The tree's form follows in two steps. Take a = diag(G) and b = (1,1,1,1) to get (tr G)^2 <= 4 SUM_A G_AA^2. Then SUM_A G_AA^2 <= SUM_AB G_AB^2, because off-diagonal squares of real entries are nonnegative.
published_hypotheses: a and b are real vectors in finite-dimensional R^n; the tree uses n = 4 and b = (1,1,1,1)
the inner product is the standard Euclidean one, and the squares are squares of real numbers
equality holds iff a and b are collinear; the extra off-diagonal step has equality iff G_AB = 0 for A != B
hypothesis_drift: ADDED, harmless (it narrows the tree's class to a subset of the theorem's): 'G symmetric'. fluctuation.py:293 encodes g[A,B] as g[min,max]. The inequality holds for every real 4x4 matrix, symmetric or not: z3 proves the non-symmetric case, and the sympy identity covers general real n x n. The tree's G is symmetric anyway, so this has no effect.

KEPT, and it matters: 'G real' (fluctuation.py:75). With complex entries and the unconjugated SUM G_AB^2, the inequality FAILS; z3 finds a counterexample with complex symmetric G and real trace. Recorded here so the hypothesis stays named.

ATTRIBUTION COMPRESSION, not a drift. fluctuation.py:75 says 'Cauchy-Schwarz gives SUM G_AB^2 >= (tr G)^2/4', which combines two steps. Cauchy-Schwarz proper gives only the diagonal bound; dropping the off-diagonal squares is a separate trivial step that needs real entries. The z3 proof at fluctuation.py:297 covers the combined statement, so nothing is lost.

The constant depends on dimension: the 1/4 is 1/n with n = 4 components (3+1 D). The tree states this correctly: 4x4 at fluctuation.py:75-79, the 2/n floor at noise.py:104-106, and T1 failing under smearing at noise.py:97.

APPLICATION hypotheses are in the file header but missing from local labels. rho = (1/2) tr G holds only for a massless, minimally coupled scalar in flat spacetime, normal-ordered against the Minkowski vacuum (fluctuation.py:15-17). Two local statements drop that qualifier: fluctuation.py:70-71 ('For ANY zero-mean quasifree (Gaussian) state') and the check label at fluctuation.py:472 ('for every zero-mean Gaussian state'). For a massive field the trace runs over n = 5 components, and the same Cauchy-Schwarz argument gives only Delta' >= 2/5. z3 shows that 1/2 fails as a bound on 5x5 matrices (SAT) and proves 2/5. Whether a physical massive state actually goes below 1/2 is not shown here.
rho != 0 is needed to form Delta'. The tree says so at fluctuation.py:91; the check here assumes tr G != 0.

rederivation.outcome:
ALL PASS, 23 checks, exit 0.
(1) Exact sum-of-squares identity (sympy expands the difference to 0) for general real n x n, n = 2 to 5: n SUM G_AB^2 - (trG)^2 = SUM_{A<B}(G_AA-G_BB)^2 + n SUM_{A!=B} G_AB^2. At n = 4 this completely proves the inequality and its equality case: every term vanishes iff G = (trG/4) I = (rho/2) I.
(2) Lagrange identity for the Cauchy-Schwarz step itself.
(3) Delta = Delta'/(1+Delta') is increasing, so Delta' >= 1/2 is equivalent to Delta >= 1/3.
(4) Controls built from rho and p_i alone reproduce the tree's printed values: thermal Delta' = 2/3; Casimir Delta' = 6 (Delta = 6/7); the same value with the sign flipped, so the bound is sign-blind; a single null mode gives Delta' = 2, Delta = 2/3.
(5) z3 checks, run independently of the tree's code: the symmetric case, the equality case and the non-symmetric case are all proved; the constant 1/4 is sharp; the equality case is attainable (vacuity guard); complex entries break the bound; 5x5 gives only 2/5.
The tree's own fluctuation.py --selftest also passes T1, T1-equality and the vacuity guard.

Leading-order decoupling: alpha_s is continuous at each heavy threshold mu = m_Q. In MSbar at one loop this is exact only at mu = m_Q; at any other mu the one-loop decoupling log ln(mu^2/m^2)/(6 pi) applies.
The scale mu lies between m_t and 'some unification scale', and the coloured content in that interval is the Standard Model's. Footnote 1: extra coloured thresholds change the relation.
Heavy-quark masses are m_Q = h_Q v, and the variation is split into Delta h_Q and Delta v.
The high-scale coupling variation is tied to Delta alpha by a GUT-dependent R. The R-term is zero when alpha_s is held fixed at the high scale, which is the tree's H1.
The light quarks u, d, s lie below every heavy threshold, so hadronic scales are described by the n_f = 3 theory.

audits.lacked_data: M's hypothesis tested for this result. b_0 = 11 - 2n_f/3 (1973) is group theory multiplied by a one-loop coefficient. It uses no measured datum, so nothing measured since (alpha_s, the quark masses, the LHC's null result on new coloured states) can move it; C_A = 3 and T_F = 1/2 are recomputed here exactly. The one-loop threshold chain (Coc et al. 2007) also uses no datum: 7/9 and 2/27 are ratios of b_0 values. What the authors left out was higher-order QCD, and that was a choice, not missing data: two-loop running and the O(alpha_s^3) decoupling constants (CKS 1997) already existed in 2007. What came later is the O(alpha_s^3) heavy-quark matrix elements (Hill-Solon 2014) and the current alpha_s(M_Z) = 0.1180(9). Having them does change the number: d ln Lambda_3/d ln v is 0.235 to 0.238, not 2/9 'EXACTLY'. That is +5.8% at NNLO (numerical RG here) and +7.3% at N3LO (Hill-Solon). It does not change the conclusions resting on the number: K_mu stays O(1) and negative, and the order-of-magnitude densities are unmoved. Evidence against M's hypothesis for this result: the one-loop value needs no data and is reproduced exactly by two routes, and the refinements are stable to within 0.1% over the alpha_s band. Evidence for it, in a weak form: the one thing that could really move the one-loop sum is the particle content between m_t and the high scale. audits.name: Unimodular gravity is classically equivalent to GR; Lambda becomes an integration constant; it does not solve the cosmological constant problem

source.located: Classic sources: Einstein 1919 (trace-free field equations), Henneaux & Teitelboim PLB 222, 195 (1989), Smolin PRD 80, 084003 (2009), Bufalo-Oksanen-Tureanu EPJC 75, 477 (2015), Fabris-Alvarenga-Velten Symmetry 15, 1392 (2023). I (sqrt(-g)=eps_0, volume-preserving diffeomorphisms, eq.(1), the 'additionally imposed' conservation sentence, the quantum/perturbative differences, the Smolin sentence) and pp.4-5, Sec. III (eqs.12-15, Lambda(R,T)=(R+kappa T)/4, the count of two vs three independent static equations). audits.published_statement: Verbatim from the restatement, arXiv:2603.14718v1 p.2: "the determinant of the spacetime metric is required to remain fixed throughout the manifold, sqrt(-g) = eps_0. This constraint reduces the full diffeomorphism invariance of GR to volume-preserving diffeomorphisms and leads to trace-free field equations in which the cosmological constant does not appear as a free parameter of the action. Instead, the divergence of the traceless field equations yields the relation R_{;nu}/4 = 8 pi G (T^{mu nu}_{;mu} - T_{;nu}/4), (1) which in general allows for a varying Lambda. Only if the conservation of the energy-momentum tensor T^{mu nu}_{;mu} = 0 is additionally imposed does the cosmological constant reduce to a constant of integration, and the full Einstein equations with a fixed Lambda are recovered. This structure implies that Unimodular Gravity and GR, while sharing the same classical field equations under this additional assumption, are known to differ at the quantum and perturbative levels." On the cosmological constant problem (p.2), Smolin's quantisation shows "vacuum energy contributions of the form g^{ab} C decouple from the gravitational dynamics, providing a concrete mechanism addressing the first cosmological constant problem." Field equations (p.5, eqs.12-15): R_mu nu - (R/4) g_mu nu = kappa (T_mu nu - T g_mu nu/4), equivalently G_mu nu + Lambda(R,T) g_mu nu = kappa T_mu nu with Lambda = (R + kappa T)/4.
published_hypotheses: H1 (defining): sqrt(-g) = eps_0 is fixed and non-dynamical, and the symmetry group is reduced to volume-preserving diffeomorphisms (2603.14718 p.2).
H2: only the trace-free part of Einstein's equations holds, eq.(12) (p.5).

H3 (load-bearing, 'additionally imposed'): T^{mu nu}_{;mu} = 0. Without it eq.(1) 'in general allows for a varying Lambda'. With it, Lambda is an integration constant and GR with a fixed Lambda is recovered (p.2).

H4 (scope): the equivalence is of the classical field equations only. The theories 'differ at the quantum and perturbative levels' (Bufalo et al. 2015, Fabris et al. 2023), and the perturbative discriminator operates 'when standard conservation laws are not imposed' (p.2).
H5 (implicit and standard; checked here, not stated in the restatement): the result is d_nu Lambda = 0, so Lambda is constant on each connected component of spacetime.
hypothesis_drift: DROPPED: H3, energy-momentum conservation. The tree states the equivalence and the integration-constant status with no conservation clause at permute.py:149-151 ('IT IS CLASSICALLY EQUIVALENT TO GENERAL RELATIVITY. Same equations, same predictions, no observation distinguishes them. What changes is what Lambda IS: an INTEGRATION CONSTANT'), permute.py:361-362 and permute.py:569-571, and again in the copies at obstruct.py:281-282, index3.py:970-971 and paper/CLAIMS.md:1103-1106, 1112, 9092-9093. The restatement makes conservation an additional hypothesis. The re-derivation's C3 witness shows the drop matters: a unimodular solution with positive-density dust, nabla.T = 1/(2 kappa t^3) != 0 and Lambda(t) = -1/(4t^2), which solves GR with a constant Lambda for no constant. Evidence the other way (C5): for matter from a diffeomorphism-invariant action, T is conserved whenever the matter equations hold, whatever the gravity equations do. So for ordinary Lagrangian matter the dropped hypothesis holds automatically.

WORDING WIDER THAN THE SCOPE: 'same predictions, no observation distinguishes them' (permute.py:149-150), 'no observation separates the two theories' (permute.py:571-573) and paper/CLAIMS.md:1106. The heading word 'CLASSICALLY' is there (permute.py:149), and with conserved T the claim holds (C2, C4d). But the restatement records a classical-perturbative discriminator when conservation is not imposed (Fabris et al.) and differences at the quantum level (Bufalo et al.). rederivation.outcome: All 13 exact symbolic checks pass (0 FAIL, sympy 1.14.0). C1: nabla^mu(R_mu nu - R g_mu nu/4) = d_nu R/4 holds identically on the general time-dependent spherical metric, which gives the restatement's eq.(1). C2: G + Lambda g - kappa T is identically the trace-free equation once Lambda := (R + kappa T)/4, matching eq.(15); with nabla.T = 0, Lambda is constant on a connected domain. C3, the witness that H3 is load-bearing: in flat FLRW with dust the trace-free system reduces to one equation, kappa rho = -2 dH/dt. With a = t^{1/2} this gives rho = 1/(kappa t^2) > 0, nabla^mu T_mu t = 1/(2 kappa t^3) != 0 and Lambda(t) = -1/(4t^2), and G_tt + Lambda0 g_tt = kappa T_tt requires Lambda0 = -1/(4t^2), so no constant Lambda works. C4, the static wormhole metric of 2603.14718 eq.(2): the trace-free system has rank 2 in (rho, p_r, p_t) and the Einstein system rank 3, agreeing with the p.5 count. Radial conservation takes the TOV form, and when the trace-free equations hold, d_r Lambda = kappa x TOV, so conservation holds exactly when Lambda is constant. C5, minimally coupled scalar: nabla^mu T_mu nu = (Box phi - V') d_nu phi. The first run failed C4c because of an index-normalisation error in this script (it multiplied by g_rr); after the fix all checks pass. Script md5 73b39856b23adf680f94ce0f1c1bed02. Output is in rederive/unimodular-gravity-classical-equivalence.out.

audits.lacked_data: This result has no measured input, so there is no datum the authors could have lacked. Its content is an identity (the contracted Bianchi identity, C1) plus one hypothesis (H3), and the identity is re-derived here exactly and agrees; no later datum can move an identity. What the tree lacked is a hypothesis, not data: conservation, which the source itself calls 'additionally imposed'. Restoring it does not change the conclusion for the tree's use, because ordinary Lagrangian matter conserves T whenever its own equations hold (C5), so within the tree's classical scope the equivalence it quotes is exact. It does change how far the statement reaches: UG admits solutions with non-conserved sources and a varying Lambda(t) that GR with a constant Lambda does not (the C3 witness). The CC sub-claim is a matter of interpretation, not data: Smolin's decoupling argument sits on one side, the free integration constant on the other. So no datum has moved; there is one dropped hypothesis, shown by computation, and one contested question flattened to a boolean.
audits.grade_evidence: The result holds exactly, but on a smaller class than the tree states. (a) The restatement (2603.14718 p.2) makes T^{mu nu}_{;mu} = 0 an additional hypothesis for both 'Lambda is an integration constant' and 'same classical field equations'. The tree drops it at permute.py:149-151, 361-362 and 569-571, and in the copies at obstruct.py:281-282, index3.py:970-971 and CLAIMS.md:1103-1106. (b) The drop matters, and it is shown here: the C3 witness (flat FLRW, a = t^{1/2}, rho = 1/(kappa t^2) > 0) solves the UG equations with nabla.T != 0 and Lambda(t) = -1/(4t^2), and solves GR with a constant Lambda for no constant. (c) Where the source's hypotheses hold (classical theory, conserved T), every step of the re-derivation agrees (C1, C2, C4). C5 puts Lagrangian matter inside that class, so the tree's use is unaffected: it is context in obstruct.py's EXPANSION-IS-A-RELABELLING row, whose verdict rests on theta = 3 H_0 and not on UG. (d) The CC-problem boolean (permute.py:363) reduces a contested question to False, while the tree's prose 'reframes rather than removes' fits the literature.
